maps.title: Gita Week · Day 01 · Why Read the Gita

nodeData.note: Bg 1.1, 1.21–30, 2.7 · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. Opening a seven-evening overview, Prabhu explains why the Gita is unique and alive, walks through Shankaracharya's Gita Mahatmya, and outlines the Gita's structure: four yogas, three sets of six chapters and five topics. He then sets the scene at Kurukshetra — Dhritarashtra's anxious question, Arjuna's breakdown on seeing his family, and his surrender to Krishna as a disciple, which Prabhu presents as the first lesson: when stuck, go to someone who knows. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: An overview: the ocean in seven days
children.note:
Prabhu calls himself only a facilitator and sets the plan: all 18 chapters in seven evenings. He compares the Gita to the ocean off Durban's beach — the further you go in, the deeper it gets, and even one verse holds many realisations.

🎙 Prabhu at 00:38 (auto-transcript): “So we're doing an overview of the Gita. That means we'll try to cover 18 chapters in the next seven days. So it is not an in-depth course because the Gita is like an ocean. you have a nice beach here in Durban right and so the ocean is very deep once you go in and you go a…”

Claiming he forgot on the way from Nairobi, Prabhu has the audience recall the basics: Krishna spoke it to Arjuna at Kurukshetra about five thousand years ago. The spot, Jyotisar, still exists, with a tree that heard the Gita.

🎙 Prabhu at 01:41 (auto-transcript): “i've forgotten right so i am pretty much sure all of you are very familiar with the gita here right uh i've just i'm just trying to remember who actually spoke the gita can anyone help me with that lord krishna okay right yes thank you and who did he speak it to arjuna and…”

Many old books stay relevant, but the Gita's unique quality is that it is alive. Prabhu points to Gandhi's words of finding comfort and fresh meaning in it, and invites everyone to try: when something bothers you, open any page and the answer is waiting at your level. — “the gita is alive”

🎙 Prabhu at 05:39 (auto-transcript): “it's the king of education it's spiritual wisdom very good but there is one very unique characteristic of the gita and that is the gita is alive right um i don't know if it's on the newer editions of the gita but i think on this one it might be there yes it is so can you read…”

children.topic: Gita Mahatmya: why we should read
children.note:
Srila Prabhupada includes Shankaracharya's glorification of the Gita. Prabhu likens it to the label on a product: as we check quality and ingredients before choosing a soap, the Mahatmya tells us why to choose the Gita.

🎙 Prabhu at 08:03 (auto-transcript): “but we should also know why should we study the Gita you've already given many answers it's relevant today it helps us with wisdom and it helps us through difficulties but in the Gita itself, Srila Prabhupada puts the words of Shankaracharya. Shankaracharya was a great…”

children.topic: Context is war, content is life
children.note:
Because it was spoken on a battlefield people assume it is about war, but Prabhu stresses that its subject is how to live. — “the context is war but the content is life”

🎙 Prabhu at 09:30 (auto-transcript): “Gita Mahatmya so we shall be going through the Gita Mahatmya and as you all said Gita was spoken on the battlefield so the context is war but the content is life it's all about life it's not about war so usually you know people expect that something is spoken on the…”

Reading the Gita brings material piety, which can lead to heaven, and spiritual piety, which takes one out of this world. Its first gift is freedom from fear and lamentation — the two words, Prabhu says, people in Johannesburg used to describe their lives.

🎙 Prabhu at 11:02 (auto-transcript): “In the first line, there is the verse, of the verse, there is the word punyam. So punyam is of two types. There is material punyam and spiritual punyam. So material punyam, punyam means pious activities, piety, means you get something good. You do something and you get…”

The Gita removes not only past sins but their reactions and the very tendency to sin. Prabhu's image: like pouring cement over a garden — no tree, no seed, and nowhere for a seed to grow. — “So the same way, with sin, Bhagavad Gita finishes it completely.”

🎙 Prabhu at 13:12 (auto-transcript): “The sin itself, the reaction for the sin and the tendency to sin, all three will be finished. So it's like you're getting rid of the tree, you're getting rid of the seeds and you're also getting rid of the possibility of putting a seed into the ground. You're getting rid of…”

children.topic: A bath that removes inner dirt
children.note:
Prabhu asks what dirt a bath in the Gita washes away. The audience names sin, impressions and the modes; he adds lust, anger, greed, illusion, madness, envy, pride and ego — all cleaned by bathing in the Gita's knowledge.

🎙 Prabhu at 14:18 (auto-transcript): “He's saying mala, dirt of material life. We can take a bath, right? Take a bath and it's done, clean. What dirt is Shankaracharya talking about over here? Sin. Okay. Yes. Very good. One is sin. What else? Past impressions. Yes. Good. What else? Modes of material nature. Modes…”

Prabhu asks where the Ganga comes from — from Lord Vishnu's feet when Vamanadeva pierced the universe. The Ganga flows from the Lord's feet and the nectar of the Gita from His mouth, and both can deliver us.

🎙 Prabhu at 16:49 (auto-transcript): “does anyone know where the ganges came from where where what is the source of the ganga where did the ganga come from lord shiva's um jata his hair okay and before that from the spiritual world yes and exactly how did that happen lord vamana very good yes Lord Vishnu Ganga's…”

children.topic: The milk of the Vedic cow
children.note:
If all Vedic knowledge were squeezed and shaped into a cow, the Gita would be its milk — the essence.

🎙 Prabhu at 18:24 (auto-transcript): “so here it's saying if you take all the vedas veda means who knows who can tell knowledge yes thank you for veda means knowledge if you take all the knowledge and squeeze it or you compress it or you make it into a cow and the essence of that knowledge is gita just like if…”

children.topic: One scripture, one God, one mantra
children.note:
Shankaracharya concludes that the Gita alone is enough: one scripture, one God, one mantra — His names — and one work, His service. Prabhu sums up the reasons to read: it is the essence of knowledge and frees us from fear and this world.

🎙 Prabhu at 20:04 (auto-transcript): “Yes, so Shankaracharya very wonderfully concludes. He says there is only one scripture and that is the Gita. You don't need any other scripture. Yes, and he wrote that even previously. So by accessing the knowledge in the Gita, it is for our benefit. We know why we are…”

The Gita holds every answer, but like Wikipedia it needs a connection. Without the internet you cannot open Wikipedia; without submission to Krishna — accepting, at least in theory, that He knows what He is saying — the Gita has no meaning. — “qualification is submissiveness. We have to be”

🎙 Prabhu at 21:35 (auto-transcript): “about the Gita is that although it is the essence of all knowledge although it contains all the answers that we will ever need we do require a special qualification to access just like nowadays there is wikipedia wikipedia is before people i'm sure you all are familiar people…”

Yoga means linking with the Supreme. Prabhu outlines karma yoga (action-based), jnana yoga (knowledge-based), bhakti yoga (devotional service) and the meditative path, and says the essence of the Gita is bhakti.

🎙 Prabhu at 23:12 (auto-transcript): “devotion or submissiveness to Krishna is required okay so we see here that Bhagavad Gita deals with four types of yoga and what is yoga yoga means connection or linking to the supreme. Whenever we find the term yoga it refers to linking with the supreme and when that yoga or…”

children.topic: Bhakti kept safe in the middle
children.note:
Like a book's front cover, middle and back, the first six chapters are karma yoga, the last six jnana, and the middle six bhakti. As we pack glass bottles in the middle of a suitcase, Krishna placed the essence in the centre. — “essence of gita he's put it right in the middle”

🎙 Prabhu at 25:08 (auto-transcript): “bhagat gita is actually bhakti yoga so just like we had seen bhagat gita has a cover front cover back cover and then the middle so 18 chapters front cover of Bhagat Gita is the first six chapters and that is known as karma yoga the back cover is the last six chapters that is…”

With the audience's help Prabhu lists the five subjects: prakriti (material nature), ishvara (God), kala (time), karma (activity) and jiva (the soul).

🎙 Prabhu at 26:29 (auto-transcript): “there are five topics so as i said you all need to help me with this um i'm kind of rusty on my five topics a bit so i'm going to ask your help on it right okay who can give us one of the topics prakriti yes okay prakriti means material nature ishwara ishwara means god kala…”
The Gita opens with the blind king asking Sanjaya what his sons and Pandu's sons did at Kurukshetra.

Using Kewal in the front row as an example, Prabhu asks: if someone came and sat for the class, would you ask what he did? Dhritarashtra's question seems pointless, but his words reveal what is in his mind.

🎙 Prabhu at 28:15 (auto-transcript): “Okay, so anyone who opens the Gita and reads this first verse, the first question may come is what sort of question is this right if I so Prabhu what's your name please if I can next to you Kival yeah okay I'm just going to use you as an example but it's not a bad example…”

Kunti accepted Nakula and Sahadeva, born of another mother, fully as her own. Dhritarashtra had a hundred sons yet still separated his five nephews from them — he wanted the kingdom.

🎙 Prabhu at 30:14 (auto-transcript): “but his thought is being expressed there first of all dhritarashtra is greedy therefore he's saying my sons and the sons of pandu see kunti marani the mother of the pandavas there were five pandavas again i'm a little bit rusty on who they are you can help me right at the…”

He doubted what would happen, feared the holy place might soften his sons into compromise, and hoped the Pandavas would give up and leave. Prabhu notes that family court cases are common today, but then such a fight was a huge thing.

🎙 Prabhu at 32:10 (auto-transcript): “but no they are different so he was greedy he wanted the kingdom what else he was also doubtful oh krishna so he was also doubtful what is exactly going to happen on the battlefield will they fight or will they compromise and therefore he was fearful about the compromise He…”

Sanjaya saw the battlefield from the palace with no wifi, Bluetooth or satellite. He reports Duryodhana's larger army and also his shock that the exiled, resourceless Pandavas had gathered such forces.

🎙 Prabhu at 34:26 (auto-transcript): “happened. So he's asking Sanjaya. Sanjaya had very advanced technology at that time. He didn't need wi-fi connection he didn't need bluetooth he didn't need dstv or any satellite but he could know exactly he was watching what was going on on the battlefield dritarashtra and…”
Arjuna asks Krishna to place his chariot between the armies so he can see who has come to fight. Prabhu asks why — he already knew his opponents — and has neighbours discuss it.

Like boxers pressing noses in a stare-down, Arjuna wanted to see his cousins' faces: were they really determined to go through with it?

🎙 Prabhu at 40:37 (auto-transcript): “arjuna wanted to see their face you know like usually in boxing matches you find that they have some weighing before they do yeah they weigh the contestants and then they have something called a stare down have you heard of it a stare down so like the contenders come to each…”

Bhishma, a devotee with an unbeaten record, fought on Duryodhana's side by Krishna's arrangement, to show that however great you are, on the wrong side you lose. — “if you are on the wrong side, you are going to lose.”

🎙 Prabhu at 41:30 (auto-transcript): “So of course before that, there was a very special player in Duryodhana's party and his name was Bishmadev. Why was he very special is because Bishmadev is a devotee of the Lord. He is a devotee of Krishna. Lord Krishna is the charioteer of Arjuna on the other side. and he is…”
Dhritarashtra's real question was who would win; Sanjaya answers it in the Gita's last verse — wherever Krishna and Arjuna are, that side wins.
Krishna points out grandfather, uncles, cousins and teachers, so Arjuna sees family instead of warriors, and his body and mind give way. Prabhu has everyone list the symptoms in these verses.

Prabhu compares it to flipping an exam paper and forgetting your own name, or fainting — and to students in India who took their lives over a paper, and couples where one quickly follows the other in death. We know this state, so the Gita is relevant.

🎙 Prabhu at 48:09 (auto-transcript): “thank you so much arjuna is experiencing all this because he's seeing his family members instead of seeing warriors and he's having a mental breakdown this happens i'm sure all of us have sat exams are going to be sitting exams exams never get over right and have you ever…”

In Kenya, fans celebrate wildly when Arsenal wins, and some have killed themselves when the team lost. A good student calms down and remembers he can re-sit; the Gita likewise puts things in perspective — it is not the end. — “But Gita puts everything in perspective.”

🎙 Prabhu at 51:57 (auto-transcript): “it's not permanent not something worth losing life over in Kenya we have fans of football I don't know here if people watch football but in Kenya they're crazy about football and when Arsenal won the cup this year whole of Kenya was red everyone came out with a red t-shirt…”

The Gita is spoken to free us from anxiety born of bodily identification. On a turbulent flight or a rocking boat everyone panics because we are out of our element; similarly this world is not our natural home, so we are always anxious.

🎙 Prabhu at 53:45 (auto-transcript): “What is the Gita there for? What does the Lord speak the Gita for? Why is it so important to us? And this is what Lord Krishna is saying here. Anshala Prabhupada is writing this in the Purput. right that the purpose of the Bhagavad Gita is to deliver the mankind from nations…”

Arjuna is no ordinary man; like a podcast host asking a diabetes doctor questions for the listeners, he takes our position. Prabhu adds Srila Prabhupada's example of the mother-in-law who scolds her daughter so that the daughter-in-law gets the message.

🎙 Prabhu at 55:46 (auto-transcript): “and Arjuna put himself in. We should not think Arjuna was an ordinary person no but just like nowadays there's podcasts isn't it and in a podcast there's an interviewer and then there's a interviewee and so sometimes the interviewer just like if you call some famous doctor…”
Overcome, Arjuna takes shelter of Krishna, admits a miserly weakness, and accepts Him as guru. Prabhu calls this the first lesson of the Gita.

An industrialist arrives at the temple in torn socks; a Gujarati keeps the plastic on the remote. A miser has resources but does not use them — Arjuna has strength and skill yet cannot use any of it.

🎙 Prabhu at 59:52 (auto-transcript): “of a miser he's a big industrialist owns lots of companies big industry but he wears torn socks true story there was one industrialist he came to the temple took out his shoes he had torn socks and we're thinking this person has torn socks that's a miser right miser you have…”

Today we approach people for a yes to our own plan. Arjuna did not come with his idea; he said 'I don't know, You tell me what is best', though nobody now likes to be told what to do. — “I need someone to say yes to my yes.”

🎙 Prabhu at 62:08 (auto-transcript): “i have come to you you tell me what is best for me say nowadays when we go to people we're looking for validation we're not really looking for some advice or some guidance you know we go to people and we ask them like oh i was thinking like this i was thinking like that i…”

Where we fail is the next sentence after 'I don't know'. Arjuna said: let me go to someone who knows. A guru takes us from confusion to clarity; when a problem is too big, ask for help. — “nowadays people say I don't know I'll figure it out”

🎙 Prabhu at 64:06 (auto-transcript): “that's where most of us fail we say i don't know what's the next statement how about you help us out what's the what's the next statement I don't know I'll figure it out Arjuna is saying I don't know let me go to someone who knows nowadays people say I don't know I'll figure…”

Krishna and Arjuna were friends, so how is this different from going to a friend? Prabhu draws out that with friends we vent and do not want advice, and we may not trust them; Arjuna fully left the decision to Krishna.

🎙 Prabhu at 66:27 (auto-transcript): “arjuna were friends right they were friends you know this krishna and arjuna were friends so when what how is this different what arjuna is doing here in this verse how is it different from us going to a friend can you discuss with the devotee sitting next to you how is…”

Questions at the end of the session.

🎙 Prabhu at 74:48 (auto-transcript): “okay very good question thank you so much for asking it madhaji is asking that arjuna had krishna right there he could go to krishna and surrender to krishna and say you know help me out here i'm stuck but who do we go to so the answer is sitting on your desk in front of you”

children.topic: Q1 · Whom do we turn to?
children.note:
A mother asks: Arjuna could surrender to Krishna in person, but where do we go?

🎙 Prabhu at 74:48 (auto-transcript): “okay very good question thank you so much for asking it madhaji is asking that arjuna had krishna right there he could go to krishna and surrender to krishna and say you know help me out here i'm stuck but who do we go to so the answer is sitting on your desk in front of you”

The answer sits on your desk. Open any page when something bugs you; the Gita is Krishna's word, so we too have Krishna in front of us. — “Gita is Krishna”

🎙 Prabhu at 75:34 (auto-transcript): “right mataji you can hold it up that's the answer yeah the gita whatever problem we have and you all can try this yeah you all can try this tonight or tomorrow morning or whenever you have something bugging you in the head just open any page of the Gita and you will find that…”

To understand the answer, read more and ask devotees you trust; that is why the community gathers to read the Gita together and see it from different angles.

🎙 Prabhu at 76:55 (auto-transcript): “For that now to understand the answer you need to read more yes or you ask other devotees around also that how can i make sense of this answer that is coming yeah it may be not your spiritual master then at least again just like arjuna had krishna as a friend someone he…”

A devotee asks why Arjuna doubted, since a kshatriya's nature is to fight.

🎙 Prabhu at 77:40 (auto-transcript): “The point you mentioned about when Krishna took Kajana between the two chariots and the two armies, so the armies were shatran by nature. So they single-minded was to fight. why would Arjuna want to see their faces why would they doubt to fight each other because Shatran…”

Arjuna knew he would win but asked at what cost, like an elder brother holding back from a younger one. Every attempt at peace had failed — Krishna Himself went, and the Pandavas asked only five villages, but Duryodhana refused land even for a needle — yet Arjuna hoped to see a flicker of doubt.

🎙 Prabhu at 78:17 (auto-transcript): “because Arjuna was a devotee and Arjuna mentions that there will be so much loss of life you know he knew yeah we're gonna fight and he knew he's going to win but he's like at what cost i will win so many of my soldiers will die so many of their soldiers will die is this all…”

nodeData.topic: Day 02 · You Are the Soul, So Work
nodeData.note: Bg 2.11–48, 3.5–9, 3.37–43 · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. Krishna's first instruction reminds Arjuna that he is the soul, not the body; Prabhu uses a touch-yourself exercise, an iPhone without a battery, AI, a dented BMW and a golden cage to show how we care for the container and forget the person inside. He then moves into the art of action: duty as a win-win, buddhi yoga, why no one can stop working, work as sacrifice (offering our food to Krishna), a karma–vikarma–akarma quiz, and lust as the enemy that drives us to sin. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: After a quick recap of day one, Prabhu describes Krishna smiling because Arjuna has finally come to his senses and asked. Then Krishna tells him that the wise grieve neither for the living nor the dead — so Arjuna, and through him we, are speaking from forgetfulness of who we are. — “you're speaking a lot of sense but actually you're speaking nonsense”

In crisis Arjuna forgot his identity and his duty, just as the student at the exam thinks failing is the end of the world.

🎙 Prabhu at 04:19 (auto-transcript): “right because we do not know who we are see in the crisis that arjuna faced on the battlefield when he saw his family members on the opposite side he went into lamentation he forgot who he was he forgot what he was supposed to do he forgot his identity or the identity can…”

Dhritarashtra, Sanjaya and Arjuna are named when they speak, but Krishna is called Bhagavan — the possessor of all strength, knowledge, beauty, fame, renunciation and wealth. Prabhu notes that Krishna is now even a unisex name; the title leaves no room for anyone to later claim to be the speaker.

🎙 Prabhu at 05:12 (auto-transcript): “And so here we see this is the first instruction in Gita of the Lord. And therefore we find the word Bhagavan Uvacha. Bhagavan. When Dhritarashtra spoke yesterday we saw it was written Dhritarashtra Uvacha. when Arjuna spoke it was written Arjuna Uvacha there is one more…”

Krishna speaks about the soul in these verses only; Arjuna understood at one hearing, but we need to hear it every day. — “You're not the body, you're the soul.”

🎙 Prabhu at 07:49 (auto-transcript): “And so Lord Krishna immediately starts by reminding Arjuna who he is And he says, you are the soul, not the body. So these are the key verses when it comes to the Gita about the soul. And these verses, they are not repeated again in the Gita. Lord Krishna speaks about the…”

Prabhu has everyone touch their nose, ear, elbow and chin — then 'touch yourself'. People point to the heart or the chest. Where are we really?

🎙 Prabhu at 08:43 (auto-transcript): “So I'd like us to do one small exercise and it's a very simple exercise. But let's see how many actually get it. So I'm going to ask you to touch a part of your bodies. And you just touch it with any hand or any how. So can everyone touch their nose? Touch your right ear.…”

Srila Prabhupada's example: a child cries that his father has gone, though the body lies right there. Prabhu adds that we have never actually seen ourselves in the mirror — only the body. What left is the soul, seen as consciousness.

🎙 Prabhu at 09:54 (auto-transcript): “Shala Prabhupada gives the example there was a small child crying and a sadhu was walking there and the sadhu asked him my dear child, why are you crying? And then the sadhu saw, oh, there was someone laying on the floor. And the child was crying, my father's gone, my…”

The newest iPhone is useless without a battery; a strong, attractive body is useless without the soul. Consciousness is the difference between living and dead.

🎙 Prabhu at 12:01 (auto-transcript): “you may have a iPhone 18 right I think that's the one that's coming out or iPhone 17 or whatever but if it has no battery inside how good is that iPhone can be the best iPhone but there's no battery inside it's useless isn't it so the same way the body may be very strong may…”

Pairs discuss the difference. A mother points to feeling, emotion and discrimination; Prabhu adds that AI chatbots hallucinate and have even encouraged suicide — they lack the awareness 'I am alive'. Thank God we have the Gita. — “artificial intelligence only hallucinates”

🎙 Prabhu at 12:39 (auto-transcript): “that is why I'm going to now ask you a question with a bit of a twist right what's the difference between AI and a human being discuss with the partner next to you AI artificial intelligence just in case some people are wondering what is AI so AI artificial intelligence and a…”

We say 'my hand', never 'I hand', yet we still suffer. When someone smashes our car's headlight we cry 'why did you hit me?' — identification makes the car's damage feel like ours. The same with our own child on the street versus the many street children we ignore: the deeper the attachment, the more the pain. — “he didn't hit you he hit the car”

🎙 Prabhu at 16:22 (auto-transcript): “attachment because of attachment yes now here in south africa you have a lot of fancy cars mercedes and bmws and someone was telling me actually you know here bmw means be my wife i don't know i don't know how true that is but it's like if you have a bmw she's the car is…”

children.topic: Feed the bird, not just the cage
children.note:
Does being the soul mean neglecting the body? No — care for it. But Prabhu lists gym sessions, protein shakes and outfit checks and asks how much of that care reaches the person inside.

🎙 Prabhu at 20:17 (auto-transcript): “soul so then the next question comes in okay we are not the body so does that mean we shouldn't take care of the body and we should just get rid of it because we are not the body we are the soul the body is not important does it mean that no so what should we do take care of…”

In Srila Prabhupada's example a lady polished her golden cage till she could see her reflection, while the bird inside starved to death. Like washing the BMW daily and forgetting breakfast. — “We take care of the car, but we forget to feed the driver.”

🎙 Prabhu at 21:35 (auto-transcript): “yeah so Srila Prabhupada gave the example of a bird in the cage and this cage was a golden cage so the owner of the cage was so happy right anyone who would come to the house oh see I have this golden cage and she would spend the whole day polishing the cage very nicely you…”

A rescuer jumps in and proudly emerges holding only the drowning man's shirt. We do the same, caring for the body, cage or car more than ourselves. — “You're saving the dress of a drowning man instead of the man himself.”

🎙 Prabhu at 23:35 (auto-transcript): “Shana Prabhupada gives another story. There was a person who was drowning. I was just seeing some clips this morning of the debris flood in Nepal. You don't want to be in that situation. The wall of rock and ice and water was just coming and swept everything away. So this…”

This verse describes the soul passing through childhood, youth and old age and then into another body. Prabhu's example: grandchildren looking at an old photo — 'this was you? where did the hair go?' — the body is different, the person the same.

The soul is never born and never dies; it only changes bodies like changing clothes. If Arjuna doesn't kill them, someone else or time will — no gym hours can save the body. — “there is bad news the body never lives”

Note down: if you audited your day, how much time goes to the body and how much to who you really are? Sometimes it is zero.

🎙 Prabhu at 27:36 (auto-transcript): “us to make a small note in our digital devices or notebooks what ways are we focusing more on the body than on the soul if you were to audit your day how much of the day is going towards taking care of the body instead of the soul you can make a small note in your notebooks…”

Arjuna might still want to prolong the relationships while the bodies last. Krishna says to tolerate separation and keep doing his duty, as we bathe in winter and cook beside a fire in summer. School best friends forever all moved on — we tolerated it.

Arjuna feared sin from killing relatives; Krishna says neglecting duty brings sin. Remember you are a soul, they are souls, and the soul cannot be killed.

🎙 Prabhu at 30:51 (auto-transcript): “tolerate the happiness or the distress that comes and move on with your duty so arjuna he didn't want to fight his duty was to fight we saw that yesterday he came to the battlefield ready to fight he didn't want to fight but krishna and he said i if i kill my relatives i'll…”
Krishna speaks a warrior's language: no physical weapon (shastra) or elemental weapon (astra) — fire, water, wind — can touch the soul.

With the audience Prabhu lists birth, growth, staying, producing by-products, dwindling and death, illustrated by a flower from bud to bloom, seed and withering. After death comes birth again — a cycle not to be disturbed by.

🎙 Prabhu at 33:24 (auto-transcript): “transformations now let's see if you can guess some of them what transformations does the body go through but okay good someone said old age yes old age growth disease is not a transformation some people may not have byproducts yes okay there's only four old age old age…”

When people move, usually it is an upgrade, and nobody cries over the old house. Arjuna's elders have old bodies and will get new ones; Krishna's last word on the soul is that it can never be killed. — “the good news is soul is ever alive”
After the knowledge, Krishna motivates with action: even if unconvinced about the soul, a warrior must fight. Arjuna saw lose-lose; Krishna reframes it — win and gain a kingdom, die and gain heaven.

Relatives would call him a coward who ran away. Prabhu contrasts this with today's cancel culture, where walking away no longer carries shame.

🎙 Prabhu at 38:32 (auto-transcript): “worse than death nowadays actually people they don't fear this so much it's called cancel culture right and they just want to cancel everything they'll run away from everything right but before people were like if if a if a student went to a exam and he returned from the…”
Krishna offers a way to act with neither good nor bad reaction, called buddhi yoga — action in Krishna consciousness — because heaven or hell, one still comes back.

Help someone and you feel proud and look for more to help — in Kenya, ten more people arrive asking. Win a svayamvara and you must marry. Good karma has repercussions too.

🎙 Prabhu at 41:19 (auto-transcript): “what does it mean that a good reaction also has some repercussions aren't we supposed to do something good so if we do good and we get a result how is that not very nice yes creates attachment can you give an example okay yes very good yeah you go and help someone you feel…”

Work without attachment to success or failure. Nobody sits an exam or interview not caring about the result, so this is hard even for Arjuna, but Krishna makes it simple: just fight. — “do the best you can do and leave the rest”

Such work brings no reaction, freedom from birth and death, and trance. Prabhu's examples: a billionaire still goes to work though his salary makes no difference, and Indian confectioners surrounded by sweets all day never eat them.

🎙 Prabhu at 47:16 (auto-transcript): “trance so it's like there's a rich person right i don't know who's on top right now is it bezos or is it elon musk okay elon musk he has enough money for his great great grandchildren to live on does he still take a salary yes he still takes a salary would it make a…”
Living in a body with bills and duties, how do we act as souls? Arjuna reasons that he needn't fight at all; Krishna answers that no one can stop working.

Prabhu asks teens and adults to sit still for two minutes; they fidget and reach for their phones. If we cannot manage two minutes, how can we not work?

🎙 Prabhu at 52:44 (auto-transcript): “there was I also do you know sessions with young adults and teens so I'd given them an exercise I told them just sit still for two minutes and I've even tried this with adults two minutes people they they go crazy they need to fidget they need to do something they check their…”
Children told to wait five minutes for a second marshmallow licked, poked and pocketed it, and most ate it. Stopping activity while the mind dwells on sense objects is pretension.

Arjuna, raised in a palace, could never live as a beggar in the Himalayas. Even maintaining the body needs work, and when we want to run away — or 'quiet quit' — Krishna says to learn how to work instead. — “Oh, what to do, I have a stomach.”
The work Krishna teaches is work done as sacrifice for Him.

children.topic: The soldier's medal, the neighbour's jail
children.note:
A soldier who kills in war gets a medal; if he kills his neighbour over a fallen apple he is arrested. One is done on authority, the other for himself. Work done for Krishna brings no reaction.

🎙 Prabhu at 59:40 (auto-transcript): “if you're a soldier in an army just like right now US and Iran are at war right so if a soldier kills an enemy soldier what do the government give him medal right they give him a medal they give him maybe more salary according to the number of enemy soldiers he killed or a…”

All eating involves killing — the mother chicken cries for her child, and even the carrot dies. If we offer vegetarian food to Krishna — leaf, flower, fruit, water — He takes away the karma, and we become prasadam eaters.

🎙 Prabhu at 62:28 (auto-transcript): “yes very good very good something we all do like he's saying we offer to lord juggernaut i'd just put a little bit of a item more in it we all eat isn't it is there anyone here who doesn't eat just checking you know sometimes you may have aliens in the crowd so we all eat…”

Printing party posters at the office, or using the company phone and fuel for yourself, is stealing. Krishna has given us earth, water, light and air; using them only for ourselves is stealing too, so offer them to Him.

Karma brings good result, vikarma bad, akarma none. Six cases: studying for high marks (karma), falsifying expenses (vikarma), cooking and offering to Krishna (akarma), donating for praise (karma), honest work offered to Krishna (akarma), dodging duty from fear (vikarma).

🎙 Prabhu at 67:46 (auto-transcript): “you get no reaction. So as I mentioned earlier, we have karma, vikarma and akarma. So karma means prescribed work, work that produces good result. If you want to remember karma, karma means good result vikarma means bad result and akarma means no result so these six questions…”
Why do people sin? Krishna answers: lust, the all-devouring enemy. It is controlled by knowledge and intelligence, which leave only work without reaction.

children.topic: Who taught the child to lie?
children.note:
No parent teaches lying, yet when a rasgulla vanishes from the table the child says 'I don't know'. Pinching at nursery, smoking and drinking need no teacher either — vikarma comes naturally. — “to sin comes naturally to us”

🎙 Prabhu at 73:09 (auto-transcript): “it pushes us to commit sin did you can see this like for children usually nobody teaches them how to lie i'm sure if your parents here do you like go and tell your child oh no no you know you should lie right nobody teaches but you just leave a rasgulla on the table and the…”
Lust sits in the senses, mind and intelligence. We cannot easily control the mind, but we can control the senses with knowledge. Tomorrow: where that spiritual intelligence comes from, chapters 4–6.

nodeData.topic: Day 03 · Knowledge That Frees Our Work
nodeData.note: Bg 4.1–9, 4.33–37, 5.10, 5.29 · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. To conquer lust we need transcendental knowledge, which comes not from our defective senses but down a line of teachers, and is knowledge of Krishna Himself — how He chooses to appear, when and why He comes, and how knowing this takes us to His eternal abode. Prabhu then explains sacrifice as work offered for Krishna's pleasure, why intention matters more than the act, the guru as the shortcut, the lotus leaf untouched by water, and peace as the doorway to happiness. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
After recalling the five truths and yesterday's thread — we are souls, we must work, lust pulls us to sin — Prabhu says lust is conquered by knowledge that comes not from universities but from beyond this world. Worldly knowledge keeps changing; he cites Darwin's theory as his example.

🎙 Prabhu at 07:33 (auto-transcript): “that's where we are today right lord krishna is saying in order to conquer lust you need knowledge but this is not ordinary knowledge where does this knowledge come from it's not that someone sat in a room and decided okay codes for living number one number two number three…”

Imperfect senses — we cannot see our own eyelids, the sun looks like a small disc, we can't tell the tea's exact temperature by touch; illusion — rope taken for a snake; the tendency to cheat; and to make mistakes. So we need a different source.

🎙 Prabhu at 10:31 (auto-transcript): “talking about right and so as Prabhu here said we as human beings we have some limitations the first one is imperfect senses and today the sound is having its own drama right imperfect senses can anyone see what's happening at the back of their head okay leave the back let's…”
Krishna says He gave this knowledge to the sun-god, and it came down from teacher to disciple, and now He gives it again to Arjuna.

Durban's best bunny chow recipe passes from mother to daughter to grandchildren by word of mouth. Transcendental knowledge is safeguarded the same way.

🎙 Prabhu at 14:26 (auto-transcript): “discipline succession just like they have what they call the family recipe or mother's recipe right and if it's one generation then it's mother's recipe and if it is more than a generation it becomes family recipe isn't it how is that recipe transmitted if there is a special…”

Students first ask a lecturer where he studied; nobody teaches without having learned from someone. Knowledge is received, not invented.

🎙 Prabhu at 15:45 (auto-transcript): “gave it to his son and in this way the knowledge comes down just like we go to university and there is a lecturer there the first question that the lecturer is asked even before he starts teaching is what are your qualifications which university did you learn from you cannot…”

To learn about the man in the front row Prabhu could guess his name, or ask his mother or brother — or simply ask him. In the Gita Krishna tells us directly who He is, so we need not speculate. — “i'll remove the guesswork out of it”

🎙 Prabhu at 17:03 (auto-transcript): “and what is this transcendental knowledge that helps us keep away from what we are not supposed to do or helps us keep away from lust this transcendental knowledge is about lord krishna himself so just like if i want to know about prabhu here who should i ask if i want to…”
The first thing Krishna tells about Himself is how He comes: by His own will, unlike us. This is the topic of Ishvara, the controller.

None of us chose our city, parents, birthday or time of birth — otherwise everyone would be born in America for the passport, and now even that is uncertain. Krishna chose all of it; we come because we are forced. — “i chose the day i chose the place i chose the parents”

🎙 Prabhu at 20:18 (auto-transcript): “did anyone choose that they would like to be if there are people here who are born in Durban did you choose to be born in Durban no really okay I'm sure you must have chosen your parents like yeah these two people are very good I'm going to come to their house no you didn't…”
He appears when irreligion rises and religion declines, and for three reasons: to protect His devotees, to destroy those who trouble them, and to re-establish religion.
Whoever understands His appearance and activities goes to His eternal abode. We are eternal but the body is not, so we need a place where we never take another body.

After a pair-share on the three reasons, Prabhu warns: never disturb Krishna's devotees, or He comes looking for you. Better to be a devotee He comes to protect. — “Trust me, we don't want to be in the number two category.”

🎙 Prabhu at 28:03 (auto-transcript): “Trust me, we don't want to be in the number two category. We should not disturb Krishna's devotees because if we disturb Krishna's devotees, then he comes looking for us and we get in trouble. So we'd rather be in the first category where we are Krishna's devotees and Krishna…”

This knowledge helps us work without reaction. Yajna is work done solely to please Krishna; lust pushes us to vikarma — no school teaches smoking or stealing — and sacrifice cleanses that sin and opens the way to His abode.

🎙 Prabhu at 28:27 (auto-transcript): “So after saying this about himself, Lord Krishna is saying this is the knowledge that you need in order to conquer lust, which will help you do your work, right? Which will help you do work, which has no reaction. So therefore he said, you do work as a sacrifice to me.…”

The eternal soul (sanatana jiva) going to the eternal Lord (sanatana ishvara) in His eternal abode (sanatana dhama) by eternal activity (sanatana dharma). Even if the rest zooms out like cars on Nairobi's expressway, remember this. — “the whole point of gita is sanatan jiva to sanatan ishvara”

🎙 Prabhu at 31:50 (auto-transcript): “so we are the soul and the other word for the soul is Sanatan, eternal Sanatan, Jiva then we saw lord krishna he is also saying i am eternal sanatan ishvara and then he says i have an eternal abode sanatan dhama and then now he's telling us how to get there and that is called…”

children.topic: Hate the boss, love the salary
children.note:
A survey: people hate their boss, their colleagues, even their work — yet stay for the pay, to enjoy. Arjuna too asks why fight with no guaranteed result; Krishna's secret is to work and forget the result.

🎙 Prabhu at 34:31 (auto-transcript): “yeah that's the only reason why we do anything there was a survey done once and they were asking people so tell us about your job right and people said I hate my boss majority of the respondents they said they hate their boss right they say we hate the boss others said we…”

children.topic: A visa for the eternal abode
children.note:
If an American visa is hard to get, imagine a visa for Sanatana-dhama. You can't buy it at a shop; you work for it, and that work is sacrifice — controlling the senses.

🎙 Prabhu at 36:21 (auto-transcript): “If you want to get visa, right? We all know how hard it is to get an American visa. If it's so hard to get an American visa, imagine a visa for Sanatan Dham. You're not going to just go to a shop and buy the visa. You have to work for it. And that work is what is known as…”

children.topic: Live to eat, or eat to live
children.note:
Prabhu met someone in Kuala Lumpur travelling the world just to taste cuisines. Most of us live to eat; the Gita says do something to get nothing, and so leave the game for Krishna's abode. — “they live to eat but geeta is telling us eat to live”

🎙 Prabhu at 37:07 (auto-transcript): “something that will please our senses i met once a person they were traveling all over the world just to eat their dream was we want to taste different cuisines right I met this person in Malaysia so I said why what are you doing here in Malaysia it's like Malaysia Kuala…”
Sacrifice in knowledge is higher than the material act. Prabhu asks which matters more, the intention or the work, and draws examples from the audience.

Srila Prabhupada's example, offered by a mother: a stranger with a knife sends us running, but we pay a surgeon to cut us. The intention makes the difference.

🎙 Prabhu at 40:51 (auto-transcript): “wanted to add something yes very good right that we go to a doctor shala prabhapad gives this example the doctor has a knife and another person has a knife if the other person comes to you with a knife and says i want to cut you up are you gonna like yes please no you are you…”

One studied hard and failed — we encourage him. The other played PS5 all night with a phone on the book — we take the console away. Same result, different intention. Study for a house in Sandton and you get only a material result.

🎙 Prabhu at 42:19 (auto-transcript): “of that work or even the work itself so say you have a child who's appearing for his secondary exam the last one and you see this child every day studying hard spending extra time learning things but then when they go to sit the exam and the results come they failed what do…”

In Srila Prabhupada's example a king visits a jail and frees a man who stole soap; nobody can stop him. Only Krishna can take away reactions, and He does so when our work is offered to Him.

🎙 Prabhu at 46:59 (auto-transcript): “Srila Prabhupada gives the example of a king going to jail. The king goes to the jail. Does it mean the king is a prisoner? No? And the king, not only is he not a prisoner, if he sees one of the inmates of the jail and he asks the person, why are you in here? Oh, my dear…”

If working as sacrifice sounds confusing, Krishna gives a shortcut: approach one who has seen the truth. That is why we hear the Gita through Srila Prabhupada — read alone, it would not make much sense.

A good teacher tells you which questions won't come in the paper. The guru explains, for example, that sacrifice means offering our work's results to Krishna. Three things are needed: serve, inquire, submit.

🎙 Prabhu at 51:01 (auto-transcript): “offering the results of our work to him and so that's a shortcut you approach a guru guru can tell you just like the teacher who's teaching a particular subject if you go to that teacher the teacher can give you some hacks isn't it right oh don't worry about this question…”

Some visitors challenge temple devotees — 'have you even gone to school?' A shopkeeper shows a polite customer the sale and discounts but tells a rude one it's out of stock; a guru likewise reveals more to a humble disciple.

🎙 Prabhu at 52:39 (auto-transcript): “to a guru why should we be submissive yes yeah submission means humility but why should we have that humility yes yeah if someone is already challenging you you'll not even want to speak to them like okay you know you do you right you keep all that drama with yourself I don't…”

A student who constantly doubts whether the university is legitimate gets little from it. Do due diligence, then approach with faith, humility, inquiry and service.

🎙 Prabhu at 54:00 (auto-transcript): “as Prabhu said there, you should have faith, yes, without faith, if you go to the university and you are always doubting, is this university a legit university, will the paper that they give me, will it be recognized is the teacher actually knowing what he is saying what…”
With knowledge of Krishna one sees things as they are, and this knowledge burns the sin and illusion that keep us here.

Krishna never says don't work. One who works without attachment and gives the results to the Lord is untouched by sin, as water glides off a waxy lotus leaf. Not detached from work, but detached in work. — “become detached in work.”

Srila Prabhupada's closest example: a mother cleans up vomit and endures kicks without expecting a million dollars or a house later. She serves regardless of the result.

🎙 Prabhu at 59:02 (auto-transcript): “Srila Prabhupada gives the example of mother and a child as the closest to what Lord Krishna is saying here when the mother has the child does the mother serve the child because she gets something from the child like oh the child vomited all over me okay it doesn't matter…”

Until the heart is purified we must work, or we drift into sin like a sacked man who uses his old keys to steal. Two drivers do the same routes for the same fare; one gives his earnings to Krishna, the other heads to the pub. Only one is implicated. — “So, the intention matters.”

🎙 Prabhu at 64:16 (auto-transcript): “two people looking exactly the same one is offering his results to Krishna and the other is not they're both doing the same work let's say they're uber drivers both of them are uber drivers they're driving the same routes they're getting the same fare but one at the end of…”

Pick an activity whose result you are attached to and find a way to offer it. A father hopes his child becomes a devotee: do your part and leave the rest to Krishna. A finance student can help the temple safeguard and grow Krishna's assets without charging devotees.

🎙 Prabhu at 66:08 (auto-transcript): “So let's do a small exercise. You all do something every day or throughout the week that you feel is very, very important, correct? Right? So can you identify one activity in which you can work in a detached way? It doesn't have to be the main activity, but is there an…”

A thief made Krishna his partner. He threw the loot at a circle, then behind a line, and each time Krishna's share was bigger; finally he threw it up, 'whatever You want, keep' — and gravity gave him everything. Make Krishna the partner in our work. — “we make Krishna a partner in our work”

🎙 Prabhu at 72:42 (auto-transcript): “right and but he understood that i can only steal if krishna lets me steal so he went to krishna and he made a deal he said we are partners okay you help me steal and whatever i get we will divide it up so somehow Krishna told him yes okay fine I am your partner so one night…”

A law-abiding South African may think the Gita doesn't apply. Yet sweeping, walking on ants and eating all take life; everyone is touched by sin, so everyone needs sacrifice.

🎙 Prabhu at 75:05 (auto-transcript): “So someone may say, no, but I don't sin. I don't sin. I'm a good, upright citizen of the Republic of South Africa. I have no criminal records. i have not harmed anyone i don't abuse anyone i don't sin so i don't need to do this right right gita is not applicable to me because…”
The result of working this way is peace, and without peace there is no happiness. Prabhu asks who wants happiness and recalls Krishna's words that the unpeaceful cannot be happy.

Sadhus doubting a saintly king were invited to a palace feast — with a sword dangling over each head. Nobody could eat. No peace, no happiness.

🎙 Prabhu at 78:46 (auto-transcript): “happy until you're peaceful so there was once a king who was saintly and there was a sadhu a saint he was wondering how can this king be saintly he is running a kingdom he is dealing with so many people how can he be saintly no no no not true let me go check him so they went…”

Peace comes from knowing Krishna is the controller, the enjoyer and our dearest friend — not the head of the family making the rules and the menu. Like a friend who insists on coming with you to a scary hospital test, Krishna comes uninvited to take us back. Like sound sleep, peace makes us happy.

🎙 Prabhu at 81:09 (auto-transcript): “And so if you want peace, Krishna is saying you need to understand three things for peace. Number one, I am the controller, not me, Krishna. Krishna is saying I am the controller. Number two, I am the enjoyer. And then number three, I am your supreme friend. We all think we…”

One question mid-class and one comment at the end.

🎙 Prabhu at 49:01 (auto-transcript): “please ask your question first yes yes very good question what happens to the sins before we actually got the knowledge and we are working with the knowledge what happens to them this knowledge is so powerful lord krishna tells us in the end of this chapter only he says this…”

A devotee asks what happens to sins committed before receiving this knowledge.

🎙 Prabhu at 49:01 (auto-transcript): “please ask your question first yes yes very good question what happens to the sins before we actually got the knowledge and we are working with the knowledge what happens to them this knowledge is so powerful lord krishna tells us in the end of this chapter only he says this…”
One spark finishes a mountain of cotton; understanding who Krishna is and why He comes burns even past sins completely.

A mother points out that we act through thoughts, words and deeds, not deeds alone.

🎙 Prabhu at 84:54 (auto-transcript): “yes yes correct very nice uh that mataji is saying”

It is not a strenuous watch over every thought. We replace thoughts with thoughts of Krishna and speech with chanting; offer work, words and thoughts, and sin slides off like water from the lotus leaf. — “our process is of replacement”

🎙 Prabhu at 86:11 (auto-transcript): “it is not a strenuous process oh what am I thinking what am I thinking oh what am I speaking What am I speaking? We don't get into it so much. Why? Because we replace it. We replace our thoughts with thoughts of Krishna and we replace our speech with chanting. So that other…”

Ink in a glass of water is removed by adding clear water until it overflows clean — not by emptying the glass. Add Krishna; you need not subtract anything.

🎙 Prabhu at 87:08 (auto-transcript): “stuff automatically is dealt with the example that is given is when you have a glass and it is filled with water and you drop a few drops of ink into it right it becomes contaminated with the ink isn't it clear water will become contaminated with the ink how do you get rid of…”

maps.title: Gita Week · Day 04 · Steady Mind, Loving Heart

nodeData.note: Bg 6.6, 6.17, 6.34–35, 6.47, 7.4–7, 7.30, 8.5–6, 9.26, 9.34 · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. Peace needs one centre — Krishna as the only hero — but the restless mind keeps us unsteady. Prabhu shows the mind as a tool like the phone, steadied by regulation, practice (chanting) and detachment; then turns to Krishna's two energies, His ownership and enjoyment of everything, remembering Him at death, and the confidential relationship of love, where He asks only a leaf, fruit, flower or water offered with love. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
After recapping the peace formula — Krishna the only enjoyer, controller and friend — Prabhu asks about movies: every story has a hero and villains. If each of us is the hero of our own movie, everyone fights. Peace comes when we see Krishna as the one hero and ourselves as supporting characters. — “there is only one hero and that is lord krishna”

🎙 Prabhu at 05:07 (auto-transcript): “we all are familiar or we have some exposure to movies isn't it so what happens in movies like any movie you take what is the general narrative arc or story that happens Keshav would you like to try yeah there is a plot twist but before the plot twist who there is always…”

Throw two stones in different places and the ripples clash; drop them in the same spot and there is no clash. Keep one centre and there is harmony.

🎙 Prabhu at 07:07 (auto-transcript): “example that Acharyas give and our devotees also normally give is like, if you go to a pond, some people have the habit of throwing stones into the pond, right? They're upset with something or they want to meditate on something, then they throw the stones in the pond. But…”

Krishna knows something in us stops us staying steady: the mind. Controlled, it is our friend; controlling us, it is our enemy. Any discipline — martial arts, university, spiritual life — needs mind control.

Pairs discuss. A five-minute social-media break becomes hours down a rabbit hole. A devotee notes the phone is a tool — used well it helps, used badly it finishes us. Replace the phone with the mind. — “are you using the phone or is the phone using you”

🎙 Prabhu at 09:36 (auto-transcript): “are you using the phone or is the phone using you ok quickly to the devotee sitting next to you or you can share it in groups of threes no problem are you using the phone or is the phone using you okay so it was a two word or maximum three word answer yeah either the former…”

After a short silence Prabhu asks what went through our minds — past, future, prasadam. He cites a study that screens have cut attention below nine seconds, which is why creators hook us in the first seconds. With thousands of thoughts, how can we think of Krishna? And lust sits in the mind. — “nine seconds that is less than a goldfish”

🎙 Prabhu at 17:07 (auto-transcript): “things go through it thousands of thoughts right there was a study done by some neuroscientists and they saw with the advent of technology especially screens before the 2010s there were not much screens. The only screen was a TV screen. People were glued to it. But with the…”
Krishna gives regulation in eating, sleeping, work and recreation as the basis for peace.

children.topic: Boxing ring, TEDx circle, tethered bull
children.note:
Friends eat breakfast in traffic, lunch at the desk, Uber Eats at night, and 'catch up' sleep at weekends — no wonder the mind is wild. Boxers stay in the ring, TEDx speakers in the red circle, a bull moves as far as its rope; the mind needs a ring too. — “and that ring is called regulation.”

🎙 Prabhu at 22:53 (auto-transcript): “mind cannot be controlled see just like when you go for a boxing match the boxers are in a ring they cannot go out of the ring whatever is happening happens in the ring or like you have a TEDx event right and in the TEDx event if you notice on the stage they have a big red…”

Hearing the dhyana-yoga method, Arjuna says the mind is harder to control than the wind. Krishna agrees and gives two tools: abhyasa, regular practice with fixed rules like school timings, and vairagya, detachment.

Our practice is chanting the maha-mantra. Mantra frees the mind — ironically by constraining it — giving it a place to rest instead of flying everywhere. — “The holy names of the Lord anchor the mind.”

🎙 Prabhu at 27:02 (auto-transcript): “Chanting of the Mahamantra. Man means mind and tra means to free the mind. Ironically, freeing the mind means constraining it, right? We usually have the opposite idea that to free the mind means there should be no restraints, no constraints. It should just be left on its…”

children.topic: No tea, no coffee: rules of detachment
children.note:
Prabhu's Sanlam colleagues couldn't compute that he took no tea, coffee, liquor or meat. The four regulative principles seem hard — a British lord once walked away from them — but they are scientific: spicy food makes a hot temper, liquor brings chaos, and like traffic rules, regulation gives freedom. — “these principles of detachment are very hard, but they're not.”

🎙 Prabhu at 29:04 (auto-transcript): “So when I was working for Sanlam, my colleagues would always ask me, we don't see you taking tea, we don't see you drinking coffee or anything, is there something, are you like lactose intolerant or something i said no i i'm not lactose intolerant i i don't take this like…”
Of all yogis, the one who always thinks of Krishna and is most connected to Him is the highest; there is no yoga without mind control.

Devotees call Krishna the Absolute Truth or Supreme Personality of Godhead rather than just 'God'. Krishna now describes His two energies: material (earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intelligence, ego) and the superior spiritual energy — us.

God as generator, operator, destroyer; the Absolute Truth is God plus His energies. A sun without light or heat is no sun; the Lord is the energetic with His energies.

🎙 Prabhu at 36:14 (auto-transcript): “right God means generator operator destroyer God generator operator destroyer and the absolute truth is God plus there is a plus and so this is Lord Krishna is telling us about the plus he's saying I'm not just generator operator destroyer no when we take the”

Pairs find both energies in the body: earth, the digestive fire, blood, breath and space are gross matter; mind, intelligence and ego are subtle but still material — no hospital can operate on them. The soul is the spiritual part.

🎙 Prabhu at 39:46 (auto-transcript): “Case in point, our body. if we look at our body I'd like you to turn to the person next to you and say how is it a combination of these two energies to the devotee next to you, can you identify how what we are seeing as the body moving and talking and going around, how is it…”

The gross body is the phone's plastic; mind, intelligence and ego are the operating system — present, but not found by breaking the phone open. Ghosts have only the subtle body; stones, water and plastic are matter alone.

🎙 Prabhu at 44:17 (auto-transcript): “material so if we were to use a different analogy lord krishna is saying the body is like the phone okay the plastic parts it's like the phone the earth water air ether they're like the plastic parts of the phone but then the mind intelligence and ego are the operating system…”
Everything is His energy, so nothing is above Him. Prabhu contrasts this emphatic statement with the reply Moses received on Sinai, 'I am who I am'.
The peace formula again, at the end of chapter 7: know Krishna as Supreme Lord and enjoyer of all sacrifices. Lordship and enjoyment go together.

Staff can't serve themselves behind the counter, but the owner can close the shop, stay open all night, or order a dish not on the menu. — “Because ownership brings enjoyment.”

🎙 Prabhu at 51:32 (auto-transcript): “say someone is working at a restaurant right and there's a lot of nice varieties of foodstuffs being made can they just go behind the counter because they're working there and just dish out one preparation for themselves no why not why not it doesn't belong to them very good…”

A chauffeur who takes his girlfriend out in the boss's Ferrari is fired. Enjoying what isn't ours is theft. We didn't make the earth; America wasn't called America 500 years ago, and the elements of any building return to the elements.

🎙 Prabhu at 52:42 (auto-transcript): “I always give the example of a chauffeur. You may be driving a very nice Mercedes S-Class. Right? Or even more like a Lamborghini or a Ferrari. But if you're a chauffeur, you can't say, okay, let me take my girlfriend out for a spin on this. The minute you do, you're fired.…”

If I give you seeds and land, can you take the whole harvest? A mother says that what is given is no longer ours; Prabhu answers it is a job given, not ownership, like the car given to a chauffeur to drive by the owner's direction.

🎙 Prabhu at 54:45 (auto-transcript): “if i give you seeds to plant right and i give you the land to plant the seeds on when it's time for the harvest the harvest belongs to who? The farmer. The farmer? Yeah. But we understand where the sauce is. Okay, so I gave you the seeds I gave you the land but the harvest…”

Krishna gives us a body as a job contract of up to a hundred years. The clever, reading the Gita, use it to return to Him; otherwise we take another contract, another body.

🎙 Prabhu at 57:18 (auto-transcript): “Krishna has given us bodies you want to do some job here fine, my place my body I am giving you a job ok, here maximum 100 years you do whatever you want to do in that 100 years and if you are clever you will not end up in jail if you read the Gita, you will not end up in…”
One who remembers Krishna at death goes to Him. And whatever we think of at death, that state we attain.

A good personal assistant isn't told to take the bus and find an Airbnb; you book two seats and the same hotel. Think of Krishna at death and you stay with Him in His abode.

🎙 Prabhu at 59:03 (auto-transcript): “he comes to my nature. My nature means my abode. He comes back to me, right? So just like if you have a personal assistant and the personal assistant does a very nice service, right? When you're flying somewhere, what usually happens? You book an air flight ticket for…”

Someone plans to enjoy now and remember Krishna at the end. But no one has an expiry label, and even knowing the date won't help: a parrot chanting 'Ram Ram' in a saintly home screamed in its natural voice when the cat caught it. What we put in comes out. — “that is what will come out”

🎙 Prabhu at 63:02 (auto-transcript): “thank you so much right there was one parrot and he was in a home of saintly people and so the parrot was chanting ram ram ram ram and everyone who would go into the house they say oh this parrot is so nice so saintly is chanting ram's name ram ram very good very nice this…”

children.topic: Always ready for the spot exam
children.note:
A student who studies daily is ready for a surprise test. Think of Krishna constantly and the time of death doesn't matter — no phone reminder can replace the work. Prabhu quotes his Guru Maharaj on shortcuts. — “in Kali Yuga, everyone is looking for a shortcut in the shortcut.”

🎙 Prabhu at 64:13 (auto-transcript): “if there is always we are thinking of Krishna then time of death doesn't matter because we are already always thinking of Krishna just like if I am continually studying for an exam and tomorrow I walk into the class and the teacher says, okay, you know, what do they call it?…”

Confidential knowledge is that we are souls; more confidential is who God is — the original 'GOAT', greatest of all time; most confidential is His relationship with His devotees, understood only by those in devotional service. — “The original OG goat is Krishna.”

Readers of the Mahabharata ask what kind of God puts His devotees through so much. Without devotional service one cannot understand it.

🎙 Prabhu at 70:17 (auto-transcript): “Many times people read the Mahabharata. And they read the Mahabharata and they say, Pandavas were devotees? Yes. Lord Krishna is the Supreme Lord? Yes. Why did the Pandavas have to suffer so much? What is this? Why did Lord Krishna take them through all that? What kind of God…”

Devotees always chant His glories, because to love someone you must know about them — like a boy who learns everything about a girl from her friends and social media. Krishna tells us His abode, names and friends. To an outsider a child pulling its mother's hair looks strange; within the relationship it makes sense.
The owner of everything asks only for these simple offerings, given with love.

children.topic: A gift for one who has everything
children.note:
Choosing gifts wrecks Prabhu's brain — you risk giving gloves to someone in the desert. All water is Krishna's, the best Iranian pomegranates are nothing to Him, and flowers today are perfumed. What He wants is love.

🎙 Prabhu at 74:08 (auto-transcript): “when people tell me about gifts and things my brain stops braining I can't figure out I can't think because to think of giving a gift to someone is really brain wrecking unless you really know or the person explicitly tells you otherwise you can go with something and then you…”

Srila Prabhupada's example: a child takes food from the father's plate and feeds him, even a half-bitten biscuit, and the father is delighted. Krishna doesn't need our love; we need Him. He gives sunlight, air and water free, and asks only that we love Him back. — “Mind you, Krishna does not need our love.”

🎙 Prabhu at 75:34 (auto-transcript): “So what is he really going for? It's the love. Shala Prabhupada gives the example of a small child the child is eating with the parents the father specifically right and he'll go to the father's plate take a morsel of food from the or food from the father's plate and feed the…”

There is nothing He won't do for His devotees: He lifted Govardhan against Indra's flood and jumped into the lake poisoned by Kaliya's fumes to protect the people of Vrindavan.

🎙 Prabhu at 79:11 (auto-transcript): “Krishna lifted a mountain ok we don't have it here do we? yeah okay yeah there Krishna lifted a mountain right there for his devotees who does that worse than Nepal floods was coming yeah Indra said we I'm going to drown the whole of Rindavan right worst flood ever in history…”

Spoken in the middle and again at the end of the Gita, this is its essence: form a relationship with Krishna, love Him and go back to Him — the way to peace, freedom from anxiety and our natural position.

Three questions at the end.

🎙 Prabhu at 82:32 (auto-transcript): “Yes, Mathiji. Is it possible to go to Krishna in this lifetime? Yes, it is. But the thing is, that's the thing. We think that the reality is something other than Krishna. And that's why Krishna is speaking the Gita to show us the reality is only Krishna. Nothing else is real.…”

A mother asks whether one can reach Krishna in this very life.

🎙 Prabhu at 82:32 (auto-transcript): “Yes, Mathiji. Is it possible to go to Krishna in this lifetime? Yes, it is. But the thing is, that's the thing. We think that the reality is something other than Krishna. And that's why Krishna is speaking the Gita to show us the reality is only Krishna. Nothing else is real.…”

Yes. The Gita shows that only Krishna is real; when our relationship with Him is real, our reality changes. Even the Pandavas, poisoned and burned out of their house, were tested — so stay with devotees who can take your hand when you lose your vision.

🎙 Prabhu at 82:54 (auto-transcript): “But the thing is, that's the thing. We think that the reality is something other than Krishna. And that's why Krishna is speaking the Gita to show us the reality is only Krishna. Nothing else is real. Only Krishna is real. Right? Everything comes from him, everything, he is…”

A mother asks about not remembering Krishna at the end.

🎙 Prabhu at 85:01 (auto-transcript): “Yes, very good. Thank you so much. Yeah, we practice, yeah, this question actually one of the disciples of Srila Prabhupada had asked him. They asked Srila Prabhupada, Srila Prabhupada, what if we don't think of Krishna at the time of death? Because they read that verse.”

A disciple asked Srila Prabhupada this; his reply was not to worry. But we must nurture the relationship every day, not be like the parrot. — “Srila Prabhupada said, don't worry, Krishna will think of you.”

🎙 Prabhu at 85:34 (auto-transcript): “Yeah, we practice, yeah, this question actually one of the disciples of Srila Prabhupada had asked him. They asked Srila Prabhupada, Srila Prabhupada, what if we don't think of Krishna at the time of death? Because they read that verse. What if we don't think, we just, you…”

If Krishna asks only for a fruit or water, why prepare elaborate meals?

🎙 Prabhu at 86:42 (auto-transcript): “okay so prabhu is asking if krishna is just asking for simple things like flower leaf water why should i prepare a 10 course meal or a 56 course meal for krishna And give him paneer and I can just give him some fruit and that's it, right? The point being Krishna is saying…”

children.topic: The bare minimum, not the limit
children.note:
Krishna set the minimum so even the poorest can come; a wealthy person shouldn't offer water and keep the feast. Whatever we eat, offer it first. A mother adds that love wants to give the best — as a loving mother cooks nicely for her child.

🎙 Prabhu at 86:59 (auto-transcript): “The point being Krishna is saying fruit, flower, but it's including whatever we can offer. He's saying you don't have to, he could have easily said give me paneer every day, right? But not everyone can do that. So he's given the bare minimum that even if someone is so poor…”
