nodeData.note: Bg 10.8–11, 11.32–33, 11.55, 12.8–12 · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. Prabhu walks through chapters 10 to 12: the four 'essence' verses of chapter 10, how to remember Krishna through everything splendid in this world, the universal form and Krishna as time, and the steps of chapter 12 by which anyone, at any level, can come to him. Stories of Srila Prabhupada's forty rupees, his heart attacks at sea, Barbarika's witness and the cat and her kitten run through the class. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Prabhu asks the hall to recall yesterday's essence: bhakti, the loving relationship between Krishna and his devotees. As sugar is naturally sweet, the soul is naturally a servant; when that service is linked to Krishna out of love, it becomes devotional service.

🎙 Prabhu at 00:30 (auto-transcript): “so yesterday we were looking at the essence of the Gita the most confidential part of the Gita so you can remind the devotee sitting next to you what was the most confidential part of the Gita or what was the essence of the Gita from yesterday's session I'll give you a hint…”

A president is elected on his promises of service, the head of a family serves the family, and even someone who serves nobody ends up serving pets. An employee serves for a salary; a devotee serves because he loves. — “So regardless of what position we may hold, our nature is to serve.”

🎙 Prabhu at 03:06 (auto-transcript): “So regardless of what position we may hold, our nature is to serve. The head of the family serves the family, right? And even if someone says, okay, I have no family, I have no country, I am living on my own I don't serve anybody yet you find that they have pets and so they…”

Light, water, air and the ground we stand on are given free. We came here wanting to forget Krishna and he even helps us forget. His love is already there; our part is only to reciprocate. — “We simply have to reciprocate.”

🎙 Prabhu at 04:59 (auto-transcript): “we had asked or we were looking at if Lord Krishna charges us for the facilities do you remember He gives us light. He gives us water. He gives us air. He gives us a place to stand on. Right? But he doesn't charge for any of this. It's free. Right? And we came here telling…”

Chapter 10, Vibhuti-yoga, shows how to see Krishna in everything. Before that, Krishna gives the catuh-sloki — four verses widely accepted as the whole Gita in summary, repeating what he said in earlier chapters.

The verse is about Krishna as the origin of the material and spiritual worlds, and the wise who understand this and worship him. Prabhu says who we are, who the Lord is and our relationship with him are all contained here.

Srila Prabhupada's example: a finger is useful only while attached to the hand and following the body. A finger lying on the road is thrown away. In the same way everything we have is Krishna's, and we are complete and happy when it is used in his service. — “unless the finger is attached to the hand”

🎙 Prabhu at 09:08 (auto-transcript): “relationship is to engage in his service. Shra Prabhupada gives the example of a finger, right? We have a finger on our hand. What is the purpose of the finger? Who can say? Yeah, to serve the body. If I want to pick up something with my finger, the finger has to obey my…”

The verse is about pure devotees whose lives are absorbed in Krishna and who find joy in speaking of him together. Prabhu stresses this is not forced labour: for devotees, life without Krishna is like a fish without water — this is why temples are built. — “For them, life without Krishna is no life.”

On the word parasparam: where is the darkest place for a lit candle? Right underneath it. Lifting it does not help; light a second candle beside it and each removes the other's darkness. That is why devotees meet and enlighten each other.

🎙 Prabhu at 12:55 (auto-transcript): “There is an example given, here you will see in the Sanskrit there is a word called Parasparam. So the example is given of a candle. If you have a candle and it's lit, what is the darkest place for that candle? If I have a candle and I light it, where is the darkest place for…”

Prabhu asks everyone to tell a neighbour what first attracted them to Krishna. Watching the room, he notices that no one is frowning — proof on the spot that talking about Krishna brings happiness.

🎙 Prabhu at 15:02 (auto-transcript): “So the devotee sitting next to you, tell them, Right. What is it that piqued your interest or attracted you to Krishna? Really quickly. The devotee sitting next to you. What is it that attracted you to Krishna? Maybe his name, maybe his form, something. okay the devotees at…”

A senior sannyasi (name as heard: Bhakti Vishrambha Madhava Swami) refused his mother's greens every day. Pulled into a temple by chanting devotees, he was served broccoli and, with everyone watching, had to eat it — and it tasted wonderful. Back home his mother could not reproduce it; later he understood the difference was that it was prasadam.

🎙 Prabhu at 16:55 (auto-transcript): “I was in one talk by His Holiness Bhakti Vishrambha Madhava Swami you may have known him He is no longer here. So he was mentioning how he came to Krishna consciousness. And he said whenever he would eat at home, the mother would always serve broccoli. In America, they call…”

Bhakti is not a lifestyle of negation. We all eat, dance and sing; we simply put Krishna in the centre, and eating becomes prasadam. — “bhakti doesn't mean we cut out a lot of things.”

🎙 Prabhu at 19:04 (auto-transcript): “So again, dear devotees, bhakti doesn't mean we cut out a lot of things. No, we simply add Krishna. We all have to eat, yes. But we add Krishna, it becomes Prasad. We all dance and chant and sing. Yes, continue doing that, but add Krishna. So it's not a negation lifestyle. It…”

The verses are about Krishna giving understanding to those who serve him with love, and himself dispelling the darkness in their hearts. Prabhu: Krishna wants us back more than we want to go. — “we take one step, Krishna takes 10 steps”

Not in dreams, Prabhu jokes. The hall answers: through the Gita, chanting, the association of devotees and the spiritual master. Through service itself Krishna gives the competence — devotees too shy to approach anyone end the day having distributed fifty or seventy books.

🎙 Prabhu at 21:50 (auto-transcript): “So, what are some of the ways how Lord Krishna facilitates this? What are some of the ways Lord Krishna gives us intelligence? Does he come in our dreams? What does it mean I give the intelligence? yes okay things you can do for him so how do we know what we can do for him…”

He went to America with forty rupees — about eight rand, Prabhu says, not even a bus fare — one contact and a box of books. In eleven years he circled the globe fourteen times, opened over 108 temples and initiated thousands. It is a science, not mumbo-jumbo. — “Srila Prabhupada had unflinching faith on Guru and Krishna”

🎙 Prabhu at 24:52 (auto-transcript): “Case in point, our founder Acharya Shala Prabhupada. Does anyone know how many rupees he went with to America? Anyone? 40 rupees. 40 rupees. That's like 8 rand I think, right? 8 rand. I don't think you can even take a public transport bus from one place to another in 8 rand.…”

The verse is about Krishna, out of compassion, destroying the ignorance in his devotee's heart. Prabhu contrasts paths like Vipassana that demand long isolation and great effort: in bhakti the devotee supplies the sincere desire to please Krishna. — “Krishna handles the rest.”

Some traditions whip or pierce themselves; devotees take prasadam four times a day. A senior devotee joked that in ISKCON no one starves — they might die of too much prasadam. Srila Prabhupada once asked a sad-looking devotee whether he was chanting, since one who chants cannot stay sad for long.

🎙 Prabhu at 30:06 (auto-transcript): “It is not that they are, you know, you find like on Easter sometimes in some countries, people are piercing themselves and whipping themselves and, you know, you've seen that. They're torturing themselves, right? Many, many traditions have this. Or like they go for vipassana,…”

Krishna lists over forty ways to see him in this world. Prabhu asks each person to think of something that fills them with awe and to look for it in chapter 10, texts 19 to 40.

🎙 Prabhu at 32:31 (auto-transcript): “And so after this, Lord Krishna gives a whole list over 42 different ways by which one can see him in this world. So most of the devotees have Bhagat Gita's in them. I would like you to think of one thing you find very beautiful in this world it can be a person but let's not…”

Answers from the hall: the banyan, with its inverted roots and huge size (Prabhu mentions a giant one in Kolkata); Uccaihsrava, the white horse from the churning of the milk ocean — 'kind of like a unicorn'; the ocean, whose size we still cannot fathom when one missing plane cannot be found; and the Surabhi cow with unlimited milk.

🎙 Prabhu at 36:06 (auto-transcript): “yes yes yes see the banyan tree can you tell us a bit about the banyan tree what's special about it the root system is inverted is that the only thing or yes and the size massive right it's not”

The verse is about all beautiful and powerful things springing from a spark of Krishna's splendour. Standing at the sea, seeing the Himalayas, the moon, the sun or a lion should trigger remembrance of him; from waking to night we can link everything to Krishna — that is Krishna consciousness.

On the ship to America Srila Prabhupada suffered two heart attacks with no doctor or hospital, yet knew he was not alone. The captain said he had never seen the Atlantic so calm and asked him to sail back with them; Prabhupada replied he had come on a one-way ticket.

🎙 Prabhu at 42:34 (auto-transcript): “Our founder Acharya Shira Prabhupada, he was on the boat or the ship going to America and he suffered two heart attacks but he still went on and reached America. Lord Krishna helped Srila Prabhupada through that difficult period can you imagine getting a heart attack on a…”

Arjuna asks for proof that Krishna is the Supreme Lord, and Krishna shows a form without beginning or end, with countless heads and arms, in which Arjuna even sees himself. Chapter 10 shows Krishna in everything; chapter 11 shows everything in Krishna. — “Chapter 11, how everything is in Krishna.”

The verse is about Krishna declaring himself time, the destroyer of worlds, and that the warriors will perish apart from the Pandavas. Prabhu: they came to Kurukshetra on one-way tickets. Empires and conquerors are gone, yet Arjuna is remembered after 5,000 years and Hanuman far longer — only devotees outlast time. — “Nobody has lasted in front of time except devotees.”

children.topic: Kitten or rat in the cat's mouth
children.note:
Prabhupada's example, recalled by a devotee: the same cat carries its kitten to safety and kills a rat. Arjuna sees warriors rushing into Krishna's mouth like moths into fire, others like rivers into the ocean. Dhruva Maharaja even stepped on the head of death.

🎙 Prabhu at 49:04 (auto-transcript): “Srila Prabhupada gives an example let's see who can get the example here of how devotees don't worry about Kalarupa it's a very famous example and I'm looking at those devotees who are seasoned amongst us not the new devotees ok I'll give you a hint it has to do something…”

The verse is about Krishna having already arranged the outcome, so Arjuna need only be his instrument and take the credit. Prabhu links it to Srila Prabhupada saying his Guru Maharaja had sent everyone to help him.

After the war the Pandavas argued over who was the greatest warrior. Krishna declined to judge and sent them to Barbarika, whose head alone had watched the whole battle. He said he saw only Krishna killing everyone on the field — then they understood the credit was theirs but the work was his.

🎙 Prabhu at 53:40 (auto-transcript): “and in fact Arjuna later on he admits to his brother right after the war was over the Pandavas they were in their tent and they were having a conversation and Bhima was saying I killed 100 sons of the Kauravas of the of Duryodhana the Kauravas I killed 100 I am the greatest…”

The verse is about the devotee who works for Krishna, holds him supreme, serves him, is free from material attachment and is friendly to all, and so comes to him. Prabhu notes chapter 9 gave four points and here there are five.

There is no agency to sign up with. Working for Krishna means doing everything to please him — opening a liquor factory 'for Krishna' does not qualify.

🎙 Prabhu at 60:02 (auto-transcript): “number one in other words what does working for krishna mean is there a agency we can go to sign up that yeah i want to work for krishna give me a position or a job is there no sure a squad yes yeah you can come to the temple say i'm signing up i want to work for krishna yes…”

On mat-parama, Prabhu offers the choice; the smiles say: Krishna, we want you — can you wait a little while we take the money? The devotee says there is nothing beyond Krishna. Avoiding company that pulls us away and being free of enmity complete the five. — “Krishna, nobody and nothing apart from you.”

🎙 Prabhu at 61:40 (auto-transcript): “if today you are asked that you can win five million rand or you can get krishna what would we choose? Judging by the smiles and the people are like Krishna we want you, can you wait just a bit can you wait just a bit we'll come back to you we'll come back to you, we promise…”

Krishna showed the universal form, the form of time, the four-armed form and finally his own two-armed form. This settles whether Vishnu comes from Krishna or the reverse: all forms come from the original two-armed Krishna.

🎙 Prabhu at 63:42 (auto-transcript): “So therefore Krishna showed that he is the source of all forms. He showed his Kala Rupa form. He showed his Vishwarupa form, his universal form, where Arjuna saw everything in Krishna. That was his universal form. And then he showed his Kalarupa form where he was eating all…”

In the middle six chapters Krishna says the same thing in different ways. Chapter 12 gives a ladder of options, and Prabhu's conclusion is that whichever step we stand on, it is not a disqualification — anyone can come to Krishna.
The verse is about fixing mind and intelligence on Krishna and so living with him. Prabhu contrasts it with mindless activity and today's corporate mindfulness exercises.

If the mind runs like a rabbit and cannot be given, practise abhyasa and vairagya, the regulative principles. Prabhupada's purport begins with rising early — and most readers, Prabhu jokes, fail right there.

Chanting, offering food or sweeping the temple are already direct devotional service, a higher level. Working for Krishna is doing one's job and giving him the result: an Uber driver sponsoring Janmashtami flowers or prasadam, or a householder providing so the family can serve Krishna. Giving all is niskama, giving part is sakama.

If inflation leaves nothing to give, try to give up some fruits of work; if not even that, cultivate knowledge of these levels, then meditate on how to offer something. Each step is better than the one below it.

Two questions after the overview.

🎙 Prabhu at 81:16 (auto-transcript): “minutes for questions if anyone has any questions or comments additions okay thank you very much Yes, okay, Mataji. Yeah. So, for devotees, when time comes,”

children.topic: Q1 · Devotees and Krishna as time
children.note:
A mataji's question (not clearly audible) about Krishna's form as time.

🎙 Prabhu at 81:34 (auto-transcript): “Yes, okay, Mataji. Yeah. So, for devotees, when time comes, Krishna comes in the form of time, devotees are not afraid. Usually when we say Krishna comes as the form of time, it means Krishna comes as death. So, devotees are not afraid of death.”

Krishna as time means death, and devotees do not fear it: like the kitten in the cat's mouth, they know it is a phase and Krishna protects them. Prabhu cites a survey where death topped people's fears, ahead of taxes, and travellers cancelling Gulf flights out of fear.

🎙 Prabhu at 81:59 (auto-transcript): “So, for devotees, when time comes, Krishna comes in the form of time, devotees are not afraid. Usually when we say Krishna comes as the form of time, it means Krishna comes as death. So, devotees are not afraid of death. They are like the kitten going in the cat's mouth. They…”

How do we know whether what happens to us is our karma or Krishna's love?

🎙 Prabhu at 84:09 (auto-transcript): “So, how do we differentiate whatever happens to us, if it's part of our karma, it's part of Krishna's love for us? It can be both. It can be both. For devotees, whatever is happening to them, they take it as Krishna's mercy. Even if it is part of their karma, they will say,…”

It can be both, but devotees take everything as mercy: a rock was due and only a pebble fell. The Pandavas suffered greatly and still said Krishna was always with them. — “They tell the problems how big Krishna is.”

🎙 Prabhu at 84:37 (auto-transcript): “For devotees, whatever is happening to them, they take it as Krishna's mercy. Even if it is part of their karma, they will say, no, Krishna is mercy. So for devotees, they say, oh, a whole rock was supposed to fall. And even if a rock did fall, they say Krishna is so…”

Krishna is the controller; if the boss decides not to open the shop, you cannot insist. Karma or not, devotees say: it is Krishna's wish.

🎙 Prabhu at 86:16 (auto-transcript): “Because remember, for the last two days we've been seeing Krishna is the controller, Krishna is the enjoyer. so if he is the controller and he wants something to happen somewhere tomorrow the boss wakes up and says we are not opening the shop you can't tell the boss no no but…”

nodeData.note: Bg 13.1–3, 13.23, 14.5, 14.26, 15.7, 15.15 · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. Opening the last six chapters, Prabhu explains the body as a field with two knowers — the soul, who knows only its own body and imperfectly, and the Supersoul, who knows every body and oversees and permits our desires. He then shows how the three modes condition everything we eat, enjoy and live in, and how bhakti alone lifts us above them, ending with Krishna in the heart as the one to be known from all the Vedas. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: Recap: three levels of confidential knowledge
children.note:
First, we are the soul, not the body; more confidential, the Lord and his energies; most confidential, the loving relationship of Krishna and his devotees — bhakti, covered in the middle six chapters. Today begins the last section, chapters 13 to 18.

🎙 Prabhu at 10:10 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna. So we looked at the most confidential part of the Gita, which is devotional service. Lord Krishna, throughout the Gita, he gives levels of confidential knowledge. The very first level of confidential knowledge was that we are the soul, not the body. and then…”

Isvara, jiva, prakriti, kala and karma in plain words: who am I, who is God, where am I, how long do I have, and what am I supposed to be doing. Only prakriti — where am I — remains, and that is today's subject. — “who am i who is god what am i supposed to be doing”

🎙 Prabhu at 13:51 (auto-transcript): “basically these five topics who am i who is god where am i that's what we look at today and what am i supposed to be doing karma and how long kala right so these are the five questions in or the five topics in very simple terms who am i who is god what am i supposed to be…”

The verses are about Arjuna's question on the field and its knower, and Krishna's answer that the body is the field and the one who knows it is the knower. Prabhu: as a farmer knows where he planted carrots, peas and beans, the soul — the dehi living in the deha — knows its own field.

We know our own headache or a stomach too full of prasadam, but not what the person beside us feels. Even our own body we know imperfectly: with food poisoning we need a doctor, and we cannot count the hairs on our head — unless we are a clean-shaven devotee. — “look at the extent of our hubris that we say, I am all knowing”

🎙 Prabhu at 17:44 (auto-transcript): “You may be sitting there and having a splitting headache, but you know you have a headache or you've eaten too much prasad and now it's feeling full. So you know, but the person next to you cannot know what's going on inside. right you know your field but you don't know the…”
The verse is about Krishna also being the knower in all bodies. Prabhu compares the individual farmer with the lands department, which knows every parcel of land in the country.

children.topic: Refuting 'I am God' in two lines
children.note:
A pair exercise: someone claims to be God — how do you answer with this verse alone? Tell me where I am hurting right now, my weight, my BMI. If you know all bodies we can talk; then show me your universal form. — “okay tell me where i'm hurting right now”

🎙 Prabhu at 22:20 (auto-transcript): “if someone tells you I am God how will you refute it using this what Lord Krishna has just said if someone comes and says I am God right how will you refute him just using this verse discuss with the partner or devotee next to you just two lines you just need to tell him two…”

Against the school that taught we are God but have forgotten, Madhvacarya would hold up two fingers: two separate knowers, soul and Supersoul — as there is man and superman. The Bhagavatam's first verse says the Absolute knows everything directly and indirectly; we know only directly, and not fully.

🎙 Prabhu at 25:11 (auto-transcript): “and so there are two knowers there are two separate knowers we have an acharya his name was Madhavacharya. Madhavacharya he was preaching very very vigorously because before him there was a school of Vedantic studies that was teaching we are God. You may hear sometimes we are…”
The verse is about the Supersoul in the body, the supreme proprietor who oversees and permits. Prabhu: when we wanted to forget him, Krishna said he would help us forget — and also come with us.

Someone who has hurt no one in this body may still suffer from acts in previous bodies. 'But who saw?' — like eating the rasagullas in an empty temple hall. Krishna says: I saw, and I permitted it because you wanted it. — “I am seeing everything”

🎙 Prabhu at 30:41 (auto-transcript): “and whatever we want to do he is giving permission so this answers the question why do bad things happen to good people i am i have not hurt anybody i have not stolen from anyone i have not actively gone and destroyed anything so why why am i suffering now right previous…”

In answer to a question: for a devotee who asks for Krishna but also something else, he can say no. As Supersoul he is official and equal — like a bank officer who cannot give a relative a loan at work. A thief and a householder both pray to him.

🎙 Prabhu at 33:40 (auto-transcript): “So that's why they say Krishna's work is very, very difficult because there is a thief praying, Krishna, please let me steal from someone's house. And then the house owner is praying, Krishna, please let no thief come. And both have to be taken care of. Both have to be taken…”

Prabhupada's examples: one who loves lying in the water all day gets a fish's body; the meat-eater a tiger's, with claws and no cooking; the heavy sleeper a bear's. Other witnesses also see — sun, moon, the demigods and Citragupta.

🎙 Prabhu at 35:18 (auto-transcript): “So Srila Prabhupada gave the example of a fish, right, there is a person he loves laying in his pool the whole day or going by the Durban beach and spending time in the water the whole day, you know. And so material nature says, why are you artificially trying to be a fish?…”

children.topic: When does the Lord step in?
children.note:
When we take up devotional service we hand agency back to him, as Arjuna did in saying he was Krishna's disciple. From then on the devotee does what Krishna wants. — “I don't know what's good for me.”

🎙 Prabhu at 36:36 (auto-transcript): “When we practice devotional service, we are giving permission to the Lord. Just like Arjuna surrendered, isn't it? I am your surrendered disciple. I don't know what is good for me. You tell me. So the moment we approach the Lord in devotional service, we are giving that…”

Desire alone is not enough: wanting a mansion without the cash gets you a smaller house. The Lord expertly mixes our desire and our karma and adjusts — perhaps a mansion in a smaller area.

🎙 Prabhu at 41:10 (auto-transcript): “So, karma is like having cash see so you have cash you want to buy a house according to the amount of cash you have you can buy a house so if you don't have that much then it can't be in very high fancy market or area right it will have to be different area because you just…”

The verse is about goodness, passion and ignorance binding the eternal soul once it contacts matter. Prabhu asks what 'conditioned' means: hot air through an air conditioner comes out cold. Guna literally means rope.

We cannot leave our body at will or fly off a tall building. Every place has conditions: shoes off for the temple hall; on a plane you may move about, but try opening the door and you are arrested. Here the condition is to stay until we want to return to Krishna.

🎙 Prabhu at 45:41 (auto-transcript): “in the prison see material nature and the world here we are bound we are bound to our bodies can anyone leave their body whenever they want like oh today I don't feel like staying in this body for today let me just jump into another one and explore and then come back no you…”

The hall places goodness in the morning, passion at noon and ignorance at night. Prabhu adds nuance — night-shift workers asleep in airport corners, the '5 a.m. club', bosses holding key meetings early — and notes that the modes are always fighting, never fixed.

🎙 Prabhu at 49:51 (auto-transcript): “sitting next to you can you try and identify the times of the day you may feel that these modes show themselves can you try the devotee sitting next to you just the time of the day as the day is progressing can you see where the mode comes it can you try and classify these…”
Eating too is governed by the modes; Krishna's purpose is to show that we are conditioned in every aspect of life.

Preaching in Burma, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura's devotees were told their puris fried in ghee smelled terrible. He sent them to the town square, where people threw dead animals into a vat and later drank from its tap. Each found the other's food repulsive — because of the modes.

🎙 Prabhu at 57:19 (auto-transcript): “Ashila Bhakti Siddhanta Sarasati Thakur was preaching in Burma. Now it's called Myanmar. And the capital is Rangoon. So they were preaching in Rangoon and in the capital, in the middle of their town square, they had a, it's called a vat. It's like this big pot with a small…”

Prabhu smiles at signs for 'fresh seafood': fresh would mean alive. Decomposed and untouchable foods belong to ignorance; food so spicy it 'burns a hole' belongs to passion; wholesome food that lengthens life belongs to goodness.

🎙 Prabhu at 60:04 (auto-transcript): “okay we know which mode you're in that which is decomposed i always find it funny i think in front here they've written fresh seafood right so how is it fresh it's dead yeah it's not fresh it's dead or they write in in nairobi also you find this they write fresh meat how is…”

Very spicy prasadam is not in passion, because it has been offered to Krishna — so do not quote the Gita at the cooks. Prabhu's uncle swore he would never give up tea, chanted anyway, and within six months refused it. — “prasad is above all these three”

🎙 Prabhu at 62:39 (auto-transcript): “prasad is above all these three doesn't matter if the prasad is very spicy It is not in the mode of passion. Why? Why? It's been offered to Krishna. It's been offered to Krishna. So Lord Krishna has taken away the reactions for that. Remember we said, when we offer work or we…”

children.topic: Homes and dress show the mode
children.note:
Goodness: clean, airy, sunlit, spacious. Passion: a room of a thousand teddy bears, walls plastered with holiday photos. Ignorance: dark, smelly, everything outside the cupboard. This knowledge is for judging our own lives, not others'.

🎙 Prabhu at 64:56 (auto-transcript): “the same applies to living if you were to apply this modes of material nature to living what would a living quarter in the mode of goodness look like neat and organized what else clean only that only two things peaceful safe no garbage in the room okay how about airy or well…”

Happiness too has three kinds. A student studies through the World Cup — poison at first, nectar when he passes; another watches every match and fails, sweetness turning to poison; a third does not care before, during or after the exam.

Pairs classify eight activities. Studying calmly is goodness; working anxiously for praise is passion; postponing duties and scrolling late at night despite exhaustion are ignorance. Places too have a 'vibe' — the temple versus the plaza half a kilometre away.

🎙 Prabhu at 72:44 (auto-transcript): “Okay, let's look at the first one. Studying calmly with a desire to understand. Goodness. Okay. I'm not hearing any other answers. So that's a pass. Right. Working anxiously for praise and recognition. Passion. Good. Repeatedly postponing an important activity or duty.…”

The verse is about unfailing devotional service taking one beyond the modes. Prabhupada's example: an iron rod left in fire becomes red-hot and burns like fire. Krishna controls the modes; by serving him we rise above them too — the temple and prasadam are not under the modes.

Srila Prabhupada lived where he had to step over people lying senseless on the floor, untouched by it. Likewise on harinama during the Ratha-yatra, devotees passed through the market without noticing it. — “he could stay there because he's connected to krishna he's above”

🎙 Prabhu at 77:51 (auto-transcript): “me lord krishna says you come up you come out then these things don't bind you anymore and therefore for someone like shala prabhapad he could stay in the bauri i have not been to the bauri but reading the descriptions of the bauri is you can understand what kind of place it…”

The verse is about living beings as Krishna's eternal fragmental parts, struggling with mind and senses under the modes. He could have let us go alone but came with us; the Gita is his knowledge to reverse-engineer our conditioning. — “we will never find satisfaction until we connect to Krishna”

The verse is about Krishna seated in every heart, giving remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness, and being the one to be known through all the Vedas. If we want to forget, he helps; if we want to remember, he helps too.

As Supersoul he is on call like a personal doctor; we dial with the maha-mantra, and he is there before we finish. Srila Prabhupada said we can give God's name, address, the way there and his personal number.

🎙 Prabhu at 83:09 (auto-transcript): “soul in the heart he's there always constantly on call right it's like having your own personal doctor, you know, on call anything, just call and he's there right, so how do we call Krishna, he's on call but we need to dial, no so what do we dial Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna…”

children.topic: Why the Gita As It Is
children.note:
Other editions carry interpretations, not in parampara — how can those who do not know Krishna explain him? Read sincerely, the Gita leaves no doubt; finishing it without knowing Krishna is supreme is like hearing the whole Ramayana and asking who Sita was.

🎙 Prabhu at 84:38 (auto-transcript): “and if we read it sincerely there is no way especially the bhagat gita as it is we don't read other gitas because other gitas why don't we read other gitas there's so many editions and so many versions yes yeah so the other gitas also krishna spoke right But why do we read…”

Read in parampara and studied nicely, the natural conclusion is that Krishna is the Supreme Lord and I am his devotee; the Gita is the milk of the Vedas. — “there is no way we will not become a devotee of Krishna.”

🎙 Prabhu at 86:27 (auto-transcript): “it's like you read you heard the whole Ramayan and then at the end of the Ramayan you ask so who was Sita? like okay what did you hear? right So, if we read Gita sincerely, if we study it nicely, there is no way we will not become a devotee of Krishna. The natural conclusion…”

Four questions from the hall.

🎙 Prabhu at 87:55 (auto-transcript): “distracted okay so i'll leave a few minutes for the questions or comments if anyone has yes prabhu there prabhu krishna is also there's some echo i can't called what Krishna is also calling our name yes he can do that he is not limited if we chant his name”

children.topic: Q1 · Does Krishna call our name?
children.note:
Partly inaudible: does Krishna also call us when we call him?

🎙 Prabhu at 88:28 (auto-transcript): “Krishna is also calling our name yes he can do that he is not limited if we chant his name then he sees who is calling me and he says oh yes so and so is calling me ok what do you want it's his number he picks it up but our problem is usually when we dial it and he picks it…”

children.topic: He picks up; we don't talk
children.note:
He is unlimited and answers at once — the problem is that, like someone who rings you and then ignores you, we dial him and then do our own thing. — “we're doing that all the time with krishna”

🎙 Prabhu at 88:52 (auto-transcript): “but our problem is usually when we dial it and he picks it up then we are not responding you know you know those people who call people and then you're like hello hello and the person is doing his own thing and you're like why did you call me we're doing that all the time…”

Do those who take up Krishna consciousness come because of association in a previous life?

🎙 Prabhu at 89:19 (auto-transcript): “Just to clarify, there is a reason how we often hear that one becomes Krishna conscious in this life because of early association in the previous lifetime with Krishna. Is that a really valid that you could have that interaction with Krishna conscious family because you may…”

Krishna does speak of an unsuccessful yogi taking birth in a pious or wealthy family to continue, but it is not required. Bhakti begins by the mercy of devotees who tell us about it. — “devotional service has no cause it's causeless”

🎙 Prabhu at 89:56 (auto-transcript): “at some point in their previous lives not necessarily lord krishna does say that for a yogi who has been practicing and didn't complete his practice then he gets another opportunity in the next life in a family of devotees or in the family of a pious person like a brahmana or…”

What happens to my soul when I sleep?

🎙 Prabhu at 91:03 (auto-transcript): “okay two things you said what happens to our soul while we sleep so who is we okay let me let me ask it in the first person what happens to my soul when i sleep right so who is i so you're asking what happens to soul when soul body is always asleep that's the point right the…”

Prabhu reframes: we are the soul. The gross body rests while the subtle body — mind, intelligence, ego — dreams of Mars or being a king; in coma both are inactive, yet breathing shows the soul is present.

🎙 Prabhu at 91:52 (auto-transcript): “a subtle body and we have a gross body so gross body is what we are seeing right now yeah subtle body is our mind intelligence and ego so that subtle body sometimes you know visits mars when we are when the gross body is inactive then the subtle body is visiting aliens and…”

Am I on this path because of the family and karma I was born with?

🎙 Prabhu at 93:21 (auto-transcript): “you had a so on a practical I would like to think that I now understand based on based on the time based on you know the family that I was born into yes experience yes based on my past karma is that true to try and say okay that was why you are on this path because lord…”

Far from India, in Africa, we speak of Krishna because Srila Prabhupada brought him here — that is Krishna's favour. Piety helps, but is not necessary; feeding prasadam gives a double dose of mercy, and a devotee can hand a book to someone outside a casino. — “bhakti is based on mercy”

🎙 Prabhu at 93:49 (auto-transcript): “path because lord krishna favored you at this time lord krishna favored you it's not that otherwise how probable is it that like even for me we're in africa far from india right ideally speaking we should have no information about krishna right few generations here no…”

nodeData.note: Bg 16.21, 18.46, 18.65–66, 18.73, 18.78 · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. In the final evening Prabhu covers chapters 16 to 18: divine and demoniac natures, the three gates of lust, anger and greed, and climbing to goodness through a regulated life and good association. He gives the 'three Rs' for turning work into worship, then the Gita's essence in 18.65–66 — think of Krishna, bow down, surrender — illustrated by Draupadi, and closes with Arjuna's resolve and Sanjaya's answer that victory lies wherever Krishna is. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Yesterday's three modes are invisible strings tying us here. Prabhu assigns colours — goodness yellow, passion red, ignorance blue — and notes that, as three primary colours mix into countless shades, three modes mix into millions of bodies.

🎙 Prabhu at 00:00 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna. So yesterday we were looking at the invisible strings that tie us to this world. And these strings are known as the gunas or the modes of material nature. And there were three of them. So the devotee sitting next to you, remind them which three strings were…”

A quiz: the cow is goodness and the lion passion; the monkey is a twist — a mix of passion and ignorance; and the elephant is ignorance, bathing for hours and then throwing mud back over itself. — “the elephant spends all its time throwing mud on itself”

🎙 Prabhu at 03:25 (auto-transcript): “to give you four animals and see if you can classify these four animals into the modes okay so i'll give them one by one and the devotee next to you you just tell them which mode you think it is so the first one is the cow okay next one the lion okay next one the monkey and…”

The four varnas reflect the modes as Prabhu presents them: teachers mainly in goodness, administrators and soldiers in passion, business people in a mix of passion and ignorance, and labourers in ignorance. Everything here is governed by the modes — but bhakti overcomes them.

🎙 Prabhu at 05:45 (auto-transcript): “occupational duties so they are known as varnas so people of a particular type of quality are in a particular type of varna so we have the brahmanas or the teachers the educators the philosophers they're primarily in which mode goodness yes and then we have the administrators…”

What is the fastest way to become a drunkard? Keep company with drunkards. Study with the toppers and you are likelier to pass. The modes we associate with take us out, keep us here or pull us deeper in.

🎙 Prabhu at 08:10 (auto-transcript): “what is the fastest way to be a drunkard to drink alcohol to join other drunkards yes you keep yourself surrounded by drunkards very quickly you'll also become one right because of the association similarly someone who wants to pass the exams if they're studying in a group…”

Bhakti Tirtha Swami used to say we each keep two dogs, a good one and a bad one; whichever we feed grows stronger.

🎙 Prabhu at 09:09 (auto-transcript): “give preference to the result will get. Bhakti Tirta Maharaj always said that our association is like having to take care of two dogs. One is a good dog and one is a bad dog. So the dog you feed will be the stronger one. If you don't give the good dog food it will starve and…”

Krishna lists 26 divine qualities — purity, knowledge, self-control, compassion, humility, truthfulness, freedom from anger, greed, envy and pride — mostly found in goodness. The demoniac nature is their opposite, with pride predominant, and grows from passion and ignorance.

A mode is known by its effect. Passion brings lust, whose whole philosophy is 'more' — one car, more; one house, more; one passport, more. Ignorance brings greed, and the two work together. — “they only have one philosophy in life”

🎙 Prabhu at 12:24 (auto-transcript): “is known by its effect. So if someone is in the mode of passion, what kind of disposition would they have if you were to give one emotion to it right if you were to give one emotion to passion what kind of disposition would a person in passion have someone said it yeah lust…”

Developing divine qualities leads out of this world; demoniac qualities keep us here. So Krishna asks us to see which modes we are associating with.

🎙 Prabhu at 14:34 (auto-transcript): “Yes. One takes us out. If we develop divine qualities, we will go out. If we develop demoniac qualities, we will go further in. We will stay here. right so therefore lord krishna is giving this knowledge that identify which mode you're associating with because that will…”

The verse is about lust, anger and greed as three gates to degradation, to be given up. Prabhu calls them brothers: when lust is frustrated, anger follows — kamanuja, lust's younger brother; when it is satisfied, greed wants one more rasagulla. Living in passion and ignorance earns first-class tickets. — “So, anger is the younger brother of lust.”

Chanting is the answer, Prabhu agrees — but not while waking at noon and eating whatever the shop opposite sells. Goodness means fixed times for waking, sleeping, eating and work; in passion people do not know right from wrong, and in ignorance they do not care. Foods in passion and ignorance increase those modes.

🎙 Prabhu at 19:48 (auto-transcript): “on the mic we should try to be regulated in our practices yes regulated in our practices and specifically regulated in our lifestyle so what lord krishna is teaching here he's not teaching some mumbo jumbo no it is a regulation of lifestyle those in the mood of goodness they…”

In ignorance we fall asleep reading the Gita — Prabhu once saw a tired devotee fall asleep while eating prasadam. Goodness is a ladder to climb; it calms anger, like the driver listening to kirtan in a traffic jam while others hoot and curse. One string is easier to break than three — and Krishna, who has no strings, can untie them all.

🎙 Prabhu at 22:09 (auto-transcript): “able to come out. And that is what Lord Krishna is suggesting. Come at least to the mode of goodness, but even the mode of goodness, eventually you will have to leave it. But to do Krishna consciousness, the mode of goodness is very conducive. In the mode of ignorance, if…”

The verse is about worshipping the Lord through one's own work. Arjuna wanted to escape to the Himalayas and beg; Krishna says running away is not the answer — do your work and worship me through it. The acaryas give a formula of three Rs.

A factory that pays 3,000 workers — righteous? The hall hesitates. Make it a liquor factory and the answer is no. Righteous work uplifts society; inflating a government tender may be good business but someone suffers. — “work that actually helps others right that is called righteous work”

🎙 Prabhu at 29:33 (auto-transcript): “a factory and i am employing 3000 people and i'm working very hard to make sure that i pay salary to those 3000 people is it righteous work how many say i don't know okay so all of you have an answer i don't know is no longer there how many say yes how many say no okay it's…”

A mataji asks whether a farm owner is responsible if workers misuse their wages. No — each is an individual. Krishna too gives us a body and facilities and the choice how to use them; we cannot blame him, nor escape our own reactions.

🎙 Prabhu at 32:24 (auto-transcript): “workers a salary but the workers they go and do unrighteous work with that salary then as a business owner or a farm owner do we get an implication yes so as a business owner do you get implicated with the activities of your employees your the unrighteous activities of your…”

Prabhu's example of a telecom launch that handed out free handsets and data: it looked like empowerment, but in his view it fed moral decay. Whatever we do should help, not damage, society.

🎙 Prabhu at 34:25 (auto-transcript): “the Ambani is in India right and a few years back they ventured into telecommunications and they started a brand called Jio and so in order to push their product they handed everyone a free handset with free internet connection okay in hindsight that is not righteous work why…”

The second R: offer the reward to Krishna, in part or in full. The third: remember him while working, as Arjuna was told to fight and remember. Often we keep the reward or forget why we are working at all. — “you fight but remember me”

🎙 Prabhu at 35:54 (auto-transcript): “righteous work number two the reward the reward of the work that we do and we get what are we doing with that so if you want to worship lord krishna through our work what should we do with the reward offer it to krishna right we give it to krishna we worked but the reward is…”

We have two sets of duties: on the bodily level, work by our nature but worship Krishna through it; on the soul level, our eternal relationship with him. Both run side by side, but the soul level must eventually take precedence.

🎙 Prabhu at 37:38 (auto-transcript): “We have two types of duties. So Lord Krishna is saying you have a body. This body is governed by modes. You work according to the karma that you have but worship me. That's one level. And then there is the higher level which we saw yesterday. We are all parts of Krishna. And…”

The verse is about always thinking of Krishna, becoming his devotee, worshipping him and offering obeisances, with his promise that one will come to him. It appeared already as 9.34; know this verse and you know the Gita's essence.

Whom do we always think of? The one we love. From postcards to video calls distance does not matter; Krishna wants us to see him everywhere — the sun as his eye, the asvattha tree, a lion in Kruger Park. Tomorrow is Janmashtami. — “we always think of the person we are attached to the person we love”

🎙 Prabhu at 40:21 (auto-transcript): “heart remember we saw in the bhakti yoga sections that who will we always think of no ordinarily speaking who do we always think of someone who sorry i heard something there who do you normally always think of someone who loves us yes thank you someone who loves us or someone…”

Become my devotee: practise bhakti-yoga, not karma, jnana or dhyana. The hall lists hearing, chanting, remembering, worship and prayer; offering fruits, flowers or a lamp — Krishna looks at the love, not the item.

🎙 Prabhu at 42:46 (auto-transcript): “your heart then he's saying become my devotee that means practice bhakti yoga no worry about karma yoga jnana yoga dhyana yoga no straight bhakti yoga and bhakti yoga has nine elements many times when we say bhakti yoga people say what is bhakti yoga right so let us help each…”

Prabhu once watched a man stride into a temple hall with his nose in the air. Some find removing fancy shoes hard, and bowing harder — we were taught to bow to no one. Yet obeisance is the easiest of the four, done right now.

🎙 Prabhu at 44:57 (auto-transcript): “one time I was sitting in a temple hall and I saw some person coming in and their nose was pointing the sky he walked into the temple hall like this everyone else comes in like this he walked okay let me come let me see what can I give Krishna no nose has to touch the ground…”

Krishna promises we will come to him; he may break his own promise but never his devotee's, so he had Arjuna declare that his devotee never perishes. Even one of the four, done perfectly, can bring us to him.

The verse is about abandoning all varieties of religion and surrendering to Krishna, who promises protection from all sinful reactions. Someone told Prabhu they were too sinful to come to the temple and would contaminate it; no sin is too great for Krishna.

Soul, karma, knowledge, meditation, the modes — and now Krishna says forget all that. The religions of the body give way to simply surrendering to him.

🎙 Prabhu at 50:56 (auto-transcript): “then he told us about karma how you should do your duty but do it with a detached manner right and then he brought us to jnana the knowledge that is required and then he spoke about meditation and the mind then he spoke about the modes and how you're supposed to deal with the…”

The problem is that surrender is counter-intuitive: all our lives we are told never give up, keep pushing, be your own boss. The devotee knows the way to win is to surrender.

🎙 Prabhu at 52:12 (auto-transcript): “the problem is we don't want to surrender right why should we surrender the whole life we go through and it's don't give up you know keep pushing and here Krishna is saying surrender and I'll take care of everything so it's counter intuitive to what we are being taught isn't…”

nodeData.topic: Gita Week — the teaching in one map
nodeData.note: Sri Gauranga Das's 7-day overview of the Bhagavad-gita As It Is, arranged by his own frame: why read it, Arjuna's crisis, the five truths (soul, work, the Lord, nature and the modes, time), the mind, knowledge and the guru, and devotion as the essence. Every bubble is a moment from the classes with its minute and a verbatim line; the link plays it. Tap Orbit for 3D; the story 'The Gita in 12 steps' is ready under ⋯ → Stories.

children.topic: The Gita is like an ocean
children.note: Like the ocean off Durban's beach, the Gita gets deeper the further you go in. Seven days can only be a brief overview, not an in-depth study. — "the Gita is like an ocean. You have a nice beach here in Durban, right?…"

children.topic: Spoken by Krishna to Arjuna at Kurukshetra
children.note: The audience recalls the basics: Krishna spoke the Gita to Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, 5,000 years ago. — "I'm just trying to remember who actually spoke the Gita. Can anyone help me with…"
The one truly unique feature: the Gita gives fresh meaning every time you open it, at whatever level you are. — "But there is one very unique characteristic of the Gita and that is the Gita…"

children.topic: Gandhi: fresh joy from it every day
children.note: Gandhi's words from the book's back cover: when doubts and disappointments come, he found comfort in the Gita and new meaning daily. — "I turn to the Bhagat Gita and find your words to comfort me. And I…"

children.topic: Open any page and find your answer
children.note: When something is bothering you, open the Gita anywhere and the answer will be there. — "open the Gita. Any page, anyhow. Not that you have to go to a specific…"

children.topic: Gita Mahatmya: why read the Gita
children.note: Prabhupada includes Shankaracharya's verses on the glories of the Gita; these give the reasons to read it. — "Shankar Achara was a great acharia for the adita school and he wrote on the…"

children.topic: Choosing soap: why choose this book
children.note: Just as we pick soap by quality, fragrance and ingredients, the Mahatmya tells us the qualities that make the Gita worth choosing. — "Let's say you're buying some soap and then you have a whole bunch of options.…"

children.topic: Context is war, content is life
children.note: Though spoken on a battlefield, the Gita is about how to live, not about warfare. — "So the context is war but the content is life. It's all about life. It's…"

Mahatmya verse 1: following the Gita frees one from bhaya (fear) and shoka (lamentation) now, and gives a spiritual next life. — "If one properly follows the instructions of how to one can be free from all…"

children.topic: Two kinds of punya: material and spiritual
children.note: Material piety takes you to heavenly planets; spiritual piety takes you out of the material world altogether. — "There is material puna and spiritual puna. So material puna puna means pious activities."

children.topic: Gita is the milk of the Vedas
children.note: Mahatmya verse 6: the Upanishads are the cow, Krishna the milker, Arjuna the calf, and the Gita is the milk for devotees to drink. — "Just like if the if you if they take the shape of a cow, then…"

children.topic: One scripture, one God, one mantra, one work
children.note: Mahatmya verse 7: one scripture (Gita), one God (Krishna), one mantra (Hare Krishna) and one work (service to the Lord). — "Let there be one scripture only. One common scripture for the whole world."

children.topic: What aspect of my life needs clarity?
children.note: A reflection exercise: write down the one area of your life you want the Gita to clarify. — "If the Gita could clarify one aspect of my life today, what aspect would that…"

Although the Gita holds all answers, they open only to someone submissive to Krishna and willing to accept him as the Supreme. — "there is a qualification that is needed and that qualification is submissiveness. We have to…"

All knowledge is online, but without a connection you cannot reach it; submissiveness is our connection to the Gita. — "in order to access that you need the internet connection isn't it without internet connection…"

The 18 chapters divide into three sets of six: karma yoga (1-6), bhakti yoga (7-12) and jnana yoga (13-18); the essence is kept in the middle. — "front cover of Bhagat Gita is the first six chapters and that is known as…"

children.topic: Medicine bottles packed in the middle
children.note: We hide what is precious in the middle of the suitcase; Krishna put bhakti, the essence, in the middle six chapters. — "If you're carrying some glass bottles of medicine or whatever in your suitcase, you don't…"

The Gita deals with five subjects: prakriti (material nature), isvara (God), kala (time), karma (activities) and jiva (the soul). — "Priti means material nature. Ishwara. Ishwara means God. Kala Kala means time."
The fourth topic, karma, covers our activities and duties. — "karma means activities or prescribed duties."

children.topic: Four yogas: linking with the Supreme
children.note: Wherever the word yoga appears it means connecting with the Supreme; the Gita covers four kinds and its essence is bhakti. — "Yoga means connection or linking to the supreme."
When the linking process is mainly work or physical activity. — "requiring some action on our part then that is known as karma yoga."
When the process is empirical, working things out with the mind. — "We're trying to figure things out with our mental capacities. Then that process is known…"

children.topic: Bhakti yoga: I am your servant
children.note: Engaging with the Lord in a devotional mood of service. — "you are the supreme lord I am your servant and that's why I'm engaging in…"

children.topic: Essence of the Gita is bhakti yoga
children.note: Of the four, devotion is the heart of the Gita. — "the essence of Bhagat Gita is actually bakti yoga."

children.topic: Arjuna: draw my chariot between the armies
children.note: Arjuna knew exactly who he would fight; he asked to see them to gauge how determined they were. — "This is in text 22 of chapter 1. He said, "Oh infallible one, please draw my chariot between the two armies so that I may see those present here who desire to fight"
No boxing match is advertised with an unknown opponent; Arjuna certainly knew his opponents. — "Muhammad Ali versus then a question mark. He'll know when he gets into the ring.…"
Like boxers staring each other down at the weigh-in, Arjuna wanted to read his cousins' faces. — "So Arjuna wanted to see how determined are my cousins to fight with me. He…"

children.topic: Bhishma: a devotee on the wrong side
children.note: Bhishma, a pure devotee with an unbeaten record, fought for Duryodhana because Krishna wanted to show that even the greatest lose on the wrong side. — "Bishma Dave is a devotey of the Lord. He he is a devotey of Krishna.…"

children.topic: On the wrong side, you lose
children.note: However great a person is, being on the wrong side means game over. — "even if you're as good as Bishma as powerful as Bishma on the battlefield if…"

children.topic: Last verse: where Krishna and Arjuna are, victory
children.note: Dhritarashtra's real question was 'who will win?'; Sanjaya answers it in the Gita's final verse. — "wherever Lord Krishna and Arjuna are that party will win."

children.topic: Arjuna's bodily symptoms on seeing family
children.note: Instead of warriors, Arjuna sees grandfather, uncle, cousin, teacher; he breaks down with about nine physical symptoms. — "So in text 28 to 30 Arjuna he is describing what he's going through when…"

children.topic: Krishna points out family, not warriors
children.note: Krishna cleverly reframed the enemy as relatives, and Arjuna's attachment took over. — ""Oh see there is your grandfather, there is your uncle, there is your cousin, there…""

children.topic: Trembling, dry mouth, hair standing on end
children.note: The list read out: limbs curling, dry mouth, trembling, hair on end, bow slipping, skin burning, unable to stand, forgetting himself, seeing only misfortune. — "My mouth is drying up. My whole body is trembling. My hair are standing on…"

children.note: No amount of gym or diet buys a guaranteed extension; every body must be destroyed by time. — "And even if someone else doesn't kill them, time will kill them. No matter how…"

children.note: Krishna speaks to the warrior in Arjuna's own language: no physical or elemental weapon can touch the soul. — "that the soul cannot be cut. That means no shastra can work acuh to the…"

children.topic: The soul can never be killed. Full stop.
children.note: Krishna's last words on the soul in the Gita; no lamentation is needed for any living being. — "He says the soul can never be killed. Full stop. Right? And therefore you do…"

children.topic: Moving house: nobody laments the old one
children.note: Grandfathers and teachers leave old bodies for new ones, an upgrade; it is cause for happiness, not grief. — "So, they had a one-bedroom house, they'll get a two or a three, right? So,…"

children.topic: Say it to your neighbour: body never alive, soul ever alive
children.note: The two-sentence conclusion each listener repeats to the devotee beside them. — "the bad news is body never alive. Body is dead. It's never alive. But the…"
Every body, human, animal or plant, goes through the same six changes; whatever is born must die. — "Birth, growth, stay for some time, produce byproducts, dwindle and then die. So everybody goes…"

children.topic: A flower: bud, bloom, seed, wither
children.note: The flower shows all six transformations in miniature. — "Take a flower for example. It's in a bud form, then it blooms. Once it…"

children.topic: After death, birth again: a cycle
children.note: Birth and death repeat; the cycle is no reason to lament or abandon duty. — "But then he's saying after death there's also birth. So this is a cycle and…"

children.topic: If not the body, why do we suffer?
children.note: The answer drawn from the audience: because of the senses and because of attachment to the body. — "But then if we know this, why do we still suffer? If I go and…"

children.topic: BMW hit on the highway: 'why did you hit me?'
children.note: The car stands for the body; nothing touched us, but attachment makes us feel every dent as pain. — "why did you hit me? Isn't it? Why did you hit me? He didn't hit…"

children.topic: Street kids vs your own kid
children.note: We ignore many street children but suffer for our own; the only difference is bodily relation and attachment. — "But if your kid ends up in the street, what happens? It's a lot of…"

children.topic: Body is the field, soul the knower
children.note: Arjuna asks about kshetra and kshetrajna; Krishna answers that the body is a field of activities and the soul living inside it is the knower of that field. — "this body or son of counti is called the field and one who knows this…"

children.topic: Dehi: the one who lives in the body
children.note: The soul is the dweller, the body the dwelling; this distinction has run through all the earlier chapters. — "Dehi means one who lives in Deha. Deha is body. So the soul lives in…"

children.topic: We are imperfect knowers even of ourselves
children.note: We know we are sick but not why; we do not know how food becomes blood or how many hairs are on our head. Our knowledge of our own field is partial. — "we ate the food we got food poisoning do we know what exactly caused the…"

children.topic: Eternal fragmental parts, struggling in the modes

Arjuna asks why fight if bodies die anyway; Krishna answers that nobody can avoid work. — "Lord Krishna is saying to Arjuna, everyone has to work. Everyone is forced to work.…"

children.note: If we cannot stay idle for two minutes, giving up work altogether is impossible. — "just sit still for 2 minutes and I've even tried this with adults. 2 minutes…"

children.note: Children who did not touch the marshmallow still thought of it constantly; not acting while dwelling on sense objects is pretending. — "And after like 4 minutes or so, most of them just ended up eating it."
Renouncing action before the heart is purified is a show; better to work. — "If you artificially stop your activities when that purification has not happened then it is…"

children.topic: Yoga: duty without attachment to results
children.note: Arjuna's refusal to fight is itself an attachment; real yoga is doing prescribed work equipoised in success and failure. — "perform your duty equipoed abandoning All attachment to success and failure that is called yoga."

children.topic: Nobody sits an exam hoping to fail
children.note: Exams and interviews show how naturally we are attached to results; even Arjuna found this hard. — "Did anyone go and sit the exam and say it doesn't matter if I pass…"

children.note: Working without expecting results brings freedom from reaction, from ritual, from rebirth, and leads to trance. — "Number two you become indifferent to the vedas. Whatever has been said, whatever has been…"

children.topic: Confectioner surrounded by sweets, no craving

children.topic: Work done as sacrifice frees from bondage
children.note: The translation read aloud: work for Krishna's satisfaction and remain free; any other work binds. — "Work done as a sacrifice has to be performed. Otherwise, work causes bondage in this…"

children.topic: Soldier gets a medal, neighbour-killer gets jail

children.topic: Practice tonight: offer your food to Krishna
children.note: We are neither vegetarians nor non-vegetarians but prasad eaters; offered food carries no karma. — "But Lord Krishna is saying if you do that as a sacrifice to me then…"

children.topic: Patram pushpam: leaf, flower, fruit, water
children.note: Krishna specifies what may be offered; whatever is offered, he takes away the karma. That is yajna. — "he gives a list patam pushpam toyam four things flowers, fruits, water and leaves you…"

children.topic: Using Krishna's facilities for ourselves is stealing
children.note: Like printing party posters on the office printer: earth, water, light and air are Krishna's resources. — "the light, he's given us the air, but instead of using it in his service,…"

One who does duty without attachment and surrenders results to the Lord is untouched by sin, as water glides off a waxy lotus leaf. — "he is not touched by sin just like a lotus leaf is not touched by…"

children.topic: Do not detach from work; be detached in work
children.note: Good or bad results both keep us stuck here, so the aim is no result at all: work without attachment. — "work. Don't run away from work but become detached in work."

children.topic: Mother serves the child expecting nothing
children.note: Prabhupada's closest example of detached service: the mother continues serving whether or not the child ever repays her. — "When the mother has the child, does the mother serve the child because she gets…"

children.topic: Intention matters more than the work
children.note: The verse on sacrifice in knowledge is read; work done with the intention of offering it to Krishna outweighs the work or its result. — "Intention behind the work is more important than the work itself."
Same act, different intention: we pay the doctor to cut us because he intends to heal. — "The doctor has a knife and another person has a knife."

children.topic: Hardworking child vs PS5 child both fail
children.note: The same failed result is treated differently by parents depending on effort and intention. — "Let's say you have another child and they're on their PS5 the whole night and…"

children.topic: We work only to enjoy the results
children.note: Sacrifice means controlling the senses: Krishna tells Arjuna to work and forget the result, which is the opposite of how we normally live. — "To achieve results. And what are you going to do with those results? Enjoy them,…"

children.topic: Survey: hate the boss, love the salary
children.note: People endure a job they hate purely for the result at the end; this shows how attached we are to results. — "we hate the boss, we hate the colleagues, and we also hate the work."
If an American visa is hard, entry to the eternal abode is earned through the work of sacrifice. — "imagine a visa for sanatan dham. You're not going to just go to a shop…"

children.topic: Live to eat vs eat to live
children.note: A traveller touring the world for cuisine stands for living for sense pleasure; the Gita reverses it - do something to get nothing. — "They live to eat. But Gita is telling us eat to live. Opposite."
