children.topic: Student studying for marks and career: karma
children.note: No one is harmed, but a result is wanted, so it is karma. — "a student studies hard because she wants admiration, high marks, and a better paying career."
Dishonest gain, even unnoticed, is forbidden action with a bad reaction. — "here so that's V karma you falsify explains claims the many salesmen usually do this…"

children.topic: Food offered to Krishna then served: akarma
children.note: Cooking with devotion and offering first produces no reaction. — "that's clearly a karma Yeah. No reaction. It's offered to Krishna and then it's fed…"

children.topic: Attain perfection by worshipping through work
children.note: Chapter 18 text 46: do the karma the Vedas give you, not sin, and it becomes worship that takes you out. — "by worship of the Lord who is the source of all beings and who is…"

children.topic: Running away is not the answer
children.note: Arjuna wanted to give up fighting and beg; Krishna insists on doing one's work and worshipping Him through it. — "I want to go to the Himalayas and beg. Lord Krishna said no you can't…"

children.topic: Three Rs turn work into worship
children.note: The acharyas' formula: righteous work, reward offered to Krishna, and remembrance of Krishna while working. — "this formula is called three R three R. So if we do these three Rs…"

Righteous is not just honest; it must actually help others rather than damage society, so inflating a government tender fails the test. — "So righteous work means work that helps others, not help myself or not help my…"

Supporting 3,000 families sounds righteous until you learn the product is liquor; the harm to society decides the answer. — "That factory is a liquor factory. So, [laughter] so now is it righteous work or…"

children.topic: Reward: offer the fruit to Krishna
children.note: The second R: whatever the work earns is given to Krishna, partly or wholly. — "We worked but the reward is yours my lord. Either in part or in full.…"
The third R: remember who the work is for. Usually one of the Rs is missing, most often remembrance. — "Lord Krishna tells Arjuna you fight on the battlefield but remember me."

children.topic: Why bad things happen to good people
children.note: Suffering in this body comes from what was done in previous bodies, and the Supersoul saw all of it. — "So this answers the question why do bad things happen to good people. I am…"
We think a wrong nobody saw does not count, but Krishna says: I saw, and I permitted it because you wanted it. — "There were too few rasgulas here in the temple hall. Nobody was there. I ate…"

children.topic: Sun, moon, demigods and Chitragupta also see
children.note: Answer to a question about Chitragupta: even if one hides from all the elements and demigods, the Lord in the heart is always there. — "The sun sees, the moon sees, other demigods see like the air etc. And then…"

children.topic: Why the speaker is called Sri Bhagavan
children.note: Dhritarashtra, Arjuna and Sanjaya are named as speakers, but Krishna's words are marked 'Sri Bhagavan uvaca'. — "There were four speakers in Gita. There's one more speaker. Apart from Arjuna darashtra and…"
Bhagavan means the one who has all strength, knowledge, beauty, fame, renunciation and wealth in full. — "One who possesses all opulences which are usually classified into six. Uh one who has…"

children.topic: Krishna chooses his birth; we do not
children.note: The verse on Krishna's appearance is read from the screen. Unlike us, the Lord is not forced to take birth; he appears by his own will. — "I chose the day. I chose the place. I chose the parents. I even chose…"

children.topic: We chose no parents, place, day, time
children.note: Nobody in the audience chose where or to whom they were born; we come because we are forced to. — "No time, no day, no place, no parents. But Lord Krishna, he's saying I am…"

children.topic: Ishvara: the Lord controls his own coming
children.note: This introduces the third of the five topics, the controller. We call ourselves controllers but control nothing about our birth. — "Now we're looking at the topic of ishwara controller. Lord controls his time to come."
To protect his devotees, to destroy those who disturb them, and to establish the principles of religion. — "Number one to deliver the pious. Number two to annihilate the miscreants. So one is…"
We want to be in the first category, protected as devotees, not in the second. — "We should not disturb Krishna's devotees because if we disturb Krishna's devotees, then he comes…"

children.topic: Absolute Truth is God plus His energies
children.note: Devotees say Absolute Truth rather than God because Krishna is described together with His energies. — "And the absolute truth is God plus. There is a plus. And so this is…"
The ordinary meaning of God; the Absolute Truth adds His energies to this. — "God means generator, operator, destroyer. G O D, right? God, generator, operator, destroyer."

children.topic: Sun with its heat and light
children.note: A sun without heat or light is no sun; the Lord is the energetic and His energies are inseparable from Him. — "So, sun plus its energies. Sun with the heat and light. Similarly, the lord has…"

Krishna describes an inferior material energy and a superior energy, the living entities, who come from Him. — "Material energy means it is made of matter or elements. Earth, water, air, fire, ether.…"

Since spirit and matter are both His energy and nothing exists outside them, Krishna is the source of everything. — "So therefore Lord Krishna is saying everything is my energy. And further on he says…"
Other scriptures lack the emphatic declaration Krishna makes about Himself in the Gita. — "I am who I am. Right? But in the Gita he's saying clearly [snorts] there…"
Chapter 10, Vibhuti-yoga, teaches how to remember Krishna by seeing Him in the things around us. — "how we can see Krishna in everything is chapter 10 Lord Krishna he tells Arjuna…"

Four verses of chapter 10 are widely accepted as the essence of the whole Gita, repeating what Krishna has been saying in earlier chapters. — "Lord Krishna gives us the entire Bhagat Gita in four shlokas. This is known as…"

children.topic: I am the source of everything
children.note: We are souls who came from Krishna; everything we have came from Krishna; so our relationship is to engage in His service. — "I am the source of all spiritual and material worlds. Everything emanates from me. The…"

children.topic: A finger is useless off the hand
children.note: The finger stands for the soul and the body for Krishna: attached and obedient, the finger is complete and happy; detached, it is thrown away. — "If I want to pick up something with my finger, the finger has to obey…"

children.topic: Pure devotees' thoughts dwell in me
children.note: Text 9: devotees do not serve begrudgingly; they get bliss from serving and from talking about Krishna with one another. — "The thoughts of my pure devotees dwell in me. Their lives are fully devoted to…"
For a devotee, life without Krishna is no life at all, just as a fish must be in water to be happy. — "for devotees living without Krishna is like a fish living without water. Fish cannot live…"

Arjuna asks Krishna to prove He is the Supreme Lord, so Krishna shows the universal form. Chapter 10 was Krishna in everything; chapter 11 is everything in Krishna. — "Krishna is telling Arjuna how he can remember him by seeing everything within this world.…"

children.topic: Time I am, destroyer of the worlds
children.note: Krishna declares Himself as time, come to destroy everyone on the battlefield except the Pandavas. — "worlds and I have come here to destroy all people with the exception of you…"

children.topic: Thousands of heads, arms and legs
children.note: In the universal form Arjuna saw all planets and demigods, and even himself, within Krishna. — "Hundreds and thousands of heads, hundreds and thousands of arms, hundreds and thousands of legs.…"
Arjuna saw the Kaurava and Pandava soldiers being devoured, became frightened, and asked who this form was. — "they were all rushing into the mouth of this form and they were being chewed.…"

children.topic: Krishna is the source of all forms
children.note: Universal form, form of time, four-handed Vishnu form and finally the original two-armed form: chapter 11 settles that Vishnu comes from Krishna, not the reverse. — "So he is the source of all forms. The forehanded, the universal, the kala rupa,…"

children.topic: The Lord is the second knower of all bodies
children.note: Besides the soul, who knows one body partially, there is a second knower, the Supreme Lord, who knows every body completely. — "there is a second knower and that is the Lord. He knows all bodies. He…"

The individual farmer knows only his own land; the lands department knows every parcel in the country. So the Lord knows all bodies while we know only ours. — "But the government official one who's working in the lands department he knows all farms…"

children.topic: Supersoul is the overseer and permitter
children.note: Krishna defines Himself in the body as the proprietor with two functions: to oversee and to permit. — "yet in this body there's another a transcendental enjoyer who is the lord the supreme…"

Out of love the Lord accompanies the soul into every body, watching everything it does and sanctioning what it wants. — "To oversee and to permit. Right? You see there are two words there overseer and…"

children.topic: Seated in the heart: remembrance and forgetfulness
children.note: Krishna in the heart supplies whichever we ask for: if we wish to forget Him He helps us forget, if we wish to remember Him He helps us remember. — "I'm seated in everyone's heart and from me comes remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness. By all…"
The Supersoul is constantly on call; we only need to dial. — "It's like having your own personal doctor, you know, on call. Anything just call and…"

children.topic: Hare Krishna is His speed dial number
children.note: Chant Hare Krishna and He is there before the mantra is even finished. — "This is his speed dial number. Just in case anyone wants to have, you know,…"

children.topic: He picks up, but we stop responding
children.note: Answer to whether Krishna also calls us: He is not limited and answers whoever calls His name; the problem is that we then do not talk to Him. — "We immediately call him, he picks up immediately and then we like oh no, now…"

children.topic: Madhva's two fingers: soul and Supersoul
children.note: Madhvacharya preached vigorously against the earlier school that taught we are God; he held up two fingers to show there are always two knowers, soul and Supersoul. — "We're two separate knowers. We have an acharia. His name was Madva."

children.topic: Two fingers means two separate knowers
children.note: Remember the two fingers: nobody should convince you after today that you are God. — "But Madvachaya used to hold up two fingers like this. Two fingers meaning two"
Supersoul means He can do what the soul cannot: He knows all bodies, not just one. — "just like we have man and then we have superman. Isn't it? So superman does…"

children.topic: Contact with nature conditions the soul
children.note: Because of desires we associate with the three modes of material nature, and this contact changes our original nature. — "Goodness, passion and ignorance. When the internality [cough] comes into contact with nature becomes conditioned…"

Conditioned means altered: as hot air is made cool by an air conditioner, the soul's original nature is changed by the modes. — "coming hot, it goes through an air conditioner and it becomes conditioned to become cool."
The modes tie the soul, and the effect depends on how much one associates with each. — "these are known as the goonas the three goonas and gona literally means rope literally…"

children.topic: Modes are the bars of the prison
children.note: We cannot leave the body at will, nor fly or eat grass in it: bound by the body and the body bound by the world. — "These are like the bars in the prison. See material nature and the world here…"

children.topic: Conditions: shoes off, seat belt, no opening the door
children.note: Entering the temple or boarding a plane carries conditions; this world's condition is that you stay until you develop the desire to return to Krishna. — "you want to come into the temple hall there's one condition what is the condition…"

children.topic: Goodness illuminates, passion binds, ignorance deludes
children.note: Three verses read aloud: goodness conditions by happiness and knowledge, passion by longing and fruitive action, ignorance by madness, indolence and sleep. — "the goodness pure love is illuminating and frees one from all sinful reactions. Those situations…"
Passion binds the soul to fruitive work through endless desire. — "The motor passion is born of unlimited size and longing both son and because of…"

children.topic: Three modes as three primary colours
children.note: Goodness is yellow, passion is red and ignorance is blue. Just as three primary colours mix into every other colour, the three modes mix into every kind of body. — "So if you were to assign these three primary colors to the modes of material…"

children.topic: Red is energetic passion, yellow calm goodness
children.note: Passion is intense activity and endless desires, so it gets red; goodness is calm and composed, so it gets yellow; ignorance gets blue. — "And yellow means calm, composed, uh cool, right? That's goodness."

children.topic: Mixed modes produce millions of bodies
children.note: Every body is a particular combination of the three modes, which is why there are so many species. — "if you combine the three modes you get combinations and according to these combinations you…"

children.topic: Morning goodness, noon passion, night ignorance
children.note: Pair exercise mapping the modes onto the day: fresh and calm in the morning, wide awake and wanting at noon, tired and lazy at night. — "Mode of goodness in the morning. Goodness in the mornings. The mode of passion at…"

children.topic: When the sun is down, inauspicious things happen
children.note: Even for night-shift workers, night generally belongs to ignorance; nobody steals in broad daylight (outside South Africa, he jokes). — "See the sun is down. So when the sun is down all sorts of inospicious…"

children.topic: Modes are always in motion, always fighting
children.note: Not a fixed rule: someone can be sleepy in the morning. One mode takes over the other two, yet a person can be mainly situated in one. — "these modes are always in motion. It is not fixed. Right. They're always in motion.…"

The verses on food read aloud: juicy, wholesome foods are goodness; bitter, spicy, burning foods are passion; stale, decomposed, putrid and untouchable foods are ignorance. — "Foods dear to those in the mode of goodness increase the duration of life, purify…"
Food in ignorance. — "Food prepared more than 3 hours before being eaten. Food that is tasteless, decomposed and…"
Attraction to these foods indicates the mode of ignorance. — "things like mushrooms, untouchable. This is fungi, right? Onion, garlic, all these things are untouchable…"

children.topic: Happiness in the modes: poison and nectar
children.note: Happiness in goodness is poison first and nectar later; in passion nectar first and poison later; in ignorance delusion from beginning to end. — "That's in which the beginning may be just like poison but at the end is…"

children.topic: Student, exams and the World Cup
children.note: In goodness he studies through the torture and passing is nectar; in passion he watches the matches and failing is poison; in ignorance he does not bother at all. — "World Cup is going on. You can't watch the match. You have to study for…"

children.topic: Three gates to hell: lust, anger, greed
children.note: Text 21 of the chapter on divine and demoniac natures: these three are the first-class tickets to hell, so avoid them and the modes that produce them. — "Lust, anger, and greed. Every sane man should give these up for they lead to…"

children.topic: Anger is the younger brother of lust
children.note: When desire is frustrated we become angry; kamanuja means the one born after lust. — "So anger is the younger brother of lust. Another name for anger is kamanuja."

children.topic: One more rasgula: greed the elder brother
children.note: When desire is fulfilled we want more; that is greed, the elder brother who always follows lust. — "Oh, that rasgula was very nice, very tasty. Can I have one more?"

children.topic: Get it: greed. Don't get it: anger
children.note: Lust comes first; both possible outcomes of a desire lead to another of the three gates. — "If we get what we want we become greedy. If we don't get what we…"

children.topic: Modes are invisible bars of a jail
children.note: The modes are also the strings that tie us; reaching goodness leaves only one string to break. — "we say this is like the modes are like the bars of the jail cell.…"

children.topic: Easier to break one rope than three
children.note: Coming to goodness reduces the bondage to one string, which is easier to break. — "it's easier to break one string than to break three, isn't it? If you have…"

children.topic: Go to Krishna, who has no strings
children.note: The easiest way out is to approach the one who is not bound by the modes at all. — "the easiest way is actually to go to a person who has no strings and…"

children.topic: Goodness is the ladder to climb out
children.note: Come at least to goodness; from there management is easier and Krishna consciousness becomes possible, even though goodness itself is eventually left behind. — "It's like a ladder. You use goodness to climb and once you reach the top…"
In ignorance you are sleepy all the time and cannot read the Gita or chant; even eating prasad becomes impossible. — "I have even seen a devotey who was so tired they fell asleep while eating…"

children.topic: Engineer your day to promote goodness
children.note: Divine qualities follow naturally when the day is redesigned around goodness. — "we have to engineer our lifestyle. We have to reinvent our day in such a…"

children.topic: Calm versus hooting in a traffic jam
children.note: Behaviour in a traffic jam shows the difference between a person in goodness and one agitated by passion. — "there people who are calm who are collected they're listening to some lecture or they're…"

One who engages in unfailing devotional service at once transcends the modes; there is no other escape. — "Lord Krishna is saying only through bacti only through devotional service can you transcend the…"

children.topic: Iron rod in fire becomes fire
children.note: By constant association with Krishna, who is above the modes, the devotee takes on Krishna's qualities, as an iron rod in fire becomes red hot and burns like fire. — "You take an iron rod and you put it in fire. Over time, what happens…"

children.topic: Bhakti is the hack, the shortcut out
children.note: Any activity of devotional service, like the temple itself, is not under the modes because it is connected to Krishna. — "bacti is like the hack it's like the means out the shortcut to come out"

A devotee connected to Krishna is not affected by degraded surroundings; likewise devotees chanting on Ratha-yatra did not even notice the market they passed. — "shap praad had to jump over people to enter his room they were lying there…"

children.topic: Desires decide which body we get
children.note: The Lord sees and records every desire and supplies a body suited to fulfil it, in sequence. — "according to our desire and according to the magnitude of our desires Lord Krishna fulfills…"

children.topic: Man who wants to live in water becomes a fish
children.note: Prabhupada's example: someone who spends all day at the Durban beach gets a fish body next life so the desire can be fulfilled naturally. — "why you artificially trying to be a fish next life we'll give you a body…"

children.topic: Meat-eater and tiger, sleeper and bear
children.note: Old Gita editions picture a meat-eater beside a tiger and a heavy sleeper beside a bear: nature gives the body that matches the desire. — "Nature will give a body where you don't have to cook anything. You just go…"
Karma dictates where we take birth and what body we get; like cash, it limits which desires can actually be bought. — "you have cash, you want to buy a house. According to the amount of cash…"

What Arjuna saw was Krishna as time. Whether Arjuna fought or not, the soldiers were already finished; only the Pandavas had return tickets. — "Krishna showed was the kala rupa the form of time. I've already killed all these…"

children.topic: I did the work, you take the credit
children.note: Krishna has already done everything; Arjuna is invited simply to act and receive the credit. — "I have already killed all these people. They're all dead. You cannot help them. But…"

Alexander, the Roman and British empires are all gone, but Arjuna and Hanuman are still spoken of; devotees conquer time. — "Pandovas 5,000 years ago, still going on. That is only 5,000. What about Lord Hanuman?…"

children.topic: This form is not for devotees
children.note: Kala-rupa destroys everyone who is not a devotee; devotees have nothing to fear from it. — "He said except the pandavas this form is not for you. It's not for the…"

children.topic: The cat, the kitten and the rat
children.note: Prabhupada's example: the same mouth of time that means death for the rat carries the kitten to safety. The devotee is the kitten. — "So, kala rupa if we equate it to the cat and then the devotey is…"

children.topic: For the rat it is a one-way ticket
children.note: The soldiers being eaten were the rat in the cat's mouth; the Pandavas were the kittens. — "But the same cat catches a rat, the rat knows now this was a one-way…"

children.topic: Moths into fire, rivers into ocean
children.note: Arjuna saw the envious (Duryodhana, Karna) rushing in like moths into fire, while the favourable (Bhishma, Drona) merged like rivers into the ocean. — "those who are enimical to Krishna but those who are favorable to Krishna he says…"

children.topic: Dhruva stood on the head of death
children.note: Dhruva Maharaja's fearlessness shows how devotees relate to time; yet, like Arjuna, they do not wish to see this form and ask for the two-armed form. — "Duva Maharaj. When death came, he stood on the head of death. He told death…"

children.topic: Remember Krishna at death, go to Krishna
children.note: Chapter 8: one who leaves the body remembering Krishna attains His nature without doubt. — "if you remember Lord Krishna at the time of death you go to Krishna At…"

children.topic: Personal assistant flies with the boss
children.note: A good assistant travels and stays with the boss; a devotee stays with Krishna in His abode. — "If the personal assistant is serving nicely, they say, oh, no, no, you know, two…"

children.topic: Whatever you think at death, you attain
children.note: Two points: a controlled mind lets us think of Krishna at death, and our final thought decides our next state. — "Whatever thoughts you have at the time of death that state you will attain"

children.topic: Can I just remember Krishna at death?
children.note: The lecturer dismantles the idea of enjoying freely now and remembering Krishna only at the end. — "I'll remember Krishna at the time of death up till that point I can do…"

children.topic: No expiry label on our heads
children.note: Death can come anytime, as the Nepal floods showed; even a Baba's astrology date does not help. — "Does anyone know when they're going to expire? Did we come with the expiry label…"
When the cat caught it, the parrot's real attachment came out; whatever we put in is what comes out at death. — "The parrot wasn't saying ram ram ram. [laughter] Yeah. Parrot was saying cow cow cow."

children.topic: Spot exam: ready because you studied daily
children.note: If we always think of Krishna, the time of death does not matter. — "Today is your spot exam, you know." Okay, I'm ready. I studied."
Chanting is already the shortcut; we still have to put in the work and make thinking of Krishna our default. — "in kalyuga everyone is looking for a shortcut cut in the shortcut. So we already…"

The verse read from the screen gives the timing of the Lord's appearance: when irreligion rises and religion declines. — "Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice or descendants of a prominent…"

Krishna tells Arjuna to fight and win glory because the outcome is already decided; Arjuna's role is only to be the instrument. — "So Lord Krishna said, "I've already dealt with everything. I've already sorted everything. You just need to be an instrument."

children.topic: Pandavas argue who was the greatest warrior
children.note: After the war Bhima, Arjuna and the brothers debated who won the battle; Krishna declined to judge and sent them to a witness. — "Bhima was saying I killed 100 sons of the koravas of of the of duryodhan…"

Bhima's son Barbarika, who watched the whole battle as a head without a body, saw only Krishna doing everything. — "he said no I could only see Krishna all over the battlefield fil killing everyone.…"

children.topic: Central message: surrender and be used
children.note: Pure devotees know they are doing nothing; Prabhupada always said his guru had sent everyone to help him. When devotees think 'I am doing', Krishna sends reminders. — "that's why he's saying nima matram become an instrument and this is the again the…"

The relationship is reciprocal and sweet; it cannot be understood without engaging in devotional service oneself. — "the harder the devotees try to serve Krishna the harder Krishna serves the devotees we…"

children.topic: Mind can be friend or enemy
children.note: Krishna's teaching in chapter 6 that the mind is the friend of one who has conquered it and the enemy of one who has not. — "Mind can be the friend and can also be the enemy. Now, how does it…"
The difference is simply who is in charge: you or the mind. — "So if we are able to control the mind then it becomes our friend. If…"

children.topic: No link with the Lord without mind control
children.note: Martial arts, studies or any spiritual path all require a controlled mind. — "We cannot link up with the supreme without mind control. Any path you take, any…"

children.topic: Are you using the phone or is it using you?
children.note: An audience exercise that sets up the mind as a tool that can either serve us or hijack us. — "Are you using the phone or is the phone using you? Okay. Quickly to the…"

children.topic: Phone hijacks time like the mind
children.note: A five-minute break becomes hours down a rabbit hole; the mind does the same thing to us. — "The phone somehow hijacks the time, isn't it? So, you have a schedule."

children.topic: Mind is a tool, like a knife
children.note: A knife or phone is good or bad depending on use; so is the mind. — "the phone is a tool. Just like here Lord Krishna will say the mind is…"

children.topic: Give the mind a ring to stay in
children.note: Boxers stay in the ring; the mind needs a boundary too. That boundary is regulation. — "So that's the frame that the speaker has to be in. Cannot leave. So we…"
The speaker's frame on stage stands for the limits regulation gives to the mind. — "The speaker or the presenter cannot go out of that red circle. Has to be…"
The rope stands for regulation that keeps the mind from running away. — "the bull can move around as much as the rope allows, but not more than…"

children.topic: Arjuna: mind harder to control than wind
children.note: Hearing the full dhyana yoga process, Arjuna protests that the flickering mind is impossible to control, and Krishna agrees it is difficult. — "It may be possible to control the wind but I find to control the mind…"

children.topic: Practice and detachment control the mind
children.note: Krishna's answer to Arjuna: abhyasa (regular practice) and vairagya (detachment). — "abiasa and vayaya these are the two tools that Lord Krishna mentions to control the…"

children.topic: Chanting the maha mantra is our practice
children.note: For devotees, abhyasa means regular chanting of Hare Krishna. — "What practice do we employ to help us control the mind? Chanting of the mahantra.…"

children.topic: Mantra frees the mind by constraining it
children.note: Man means mind, tra means to free; the holy names anchor the mind and give it a place to rest. — "Ironically freeing the mind means constraining it. Right? We are we usually have the opposite…"

children.topic: Rules of detachment in our lifestyle
children.note: Vairagya for devotees means the regulative principles: no tea, coffee, liquor, meat, eggs or fish. — "There are some rules and regulations we give to ourselves in our lifestyle that help…"

children.topic: British lord who wanted to be a brahmana
children.note: People find the principles hard only because they lack the right frame; with it they are not hard at all. — "can make you a brahmana no follow these four rules. And then the Lord said…"
Krishna's method for controlling the mind begins with a regulated lifestyle. — "So one who is regulated in his eating vihara means to sleep. One who is…"

children.topic: Breakfast in traffic, lunch at the desk
children.note: Modern life with no fixed time or diet for eating makes the mind impossible to control. — "they're having breakfast in traffic because they got late. Yeah. Either they have some coffee…"

children.topic: Catching up sleep on the weekend
children.note: Irregular sleep, early, late or none at all, keeps the mind unsteady. — "So I spent the weekend catching up my sleep, right? It doesn't work that way…"
Arjuna asks why people do what they should not; Krishna names lust as the driver. — "Arjuna is saying why do people do v karma? Why do they want to perform…"

children.topic: All-devouring sinful enemy of the world
children.note: Controlled by intelligence and knowledge, lust stops vikarma and karma so only akarma remains. — "See lust is very very it's the all devouring sinful enemy of the world. It…"
Nobody teaches a child to lie; sin comes naturally because lust is already within. — "you just leave a rasgula on the table and the child is roaming around and…"

children.topic: Control senses by knowledge, steady the mind
children.note: The closing point; where that spiritual intelligence comes from is tomorrow's topic (chapters 4-6). — "if you control the senses through knowledge then lust comes under control and that's why…"

children.topic: Mind is the sitting place of lust
children.note: An uncontrolled mind becomes an enemy that pulls us from what we should do, just as lust did in chapter 3. — "the mind is also a sitting place of lust. Lust sits in the mind. So…"

children.topic: Four defects of the conditioned human
children.note: Imperfect senses, the tendency to be illusioned, the tendency to cheat and the tendency to make mistakes - so knowledge from this world cannot be trusted as a final source. — "we as human beings we have some limitations the first one is imperfect senses"

children.topic: We cannot even see our own eyelids
children.note: Stands for imperfect senses: we acquire knowledge through senses that cannot even measure exactly how hot a cup of tea is. — "We have eyes, but we can't see even our own eyelids. So, we're limited by…"
Stands for the tendency to be illusioned: we do not see reality as it is. — "We see a rope lying on the floor from afar. We may think it's a…"
The third defect: presenting guesswork as fact to the whole world. — "we tend to cheat also just like Charles Darwin sat in Galapagos Islands"
The fourth defect; to err is human, so we must trust knowledge from a different source. — "Is there anybody here who has never made a mistake in their life? Now we've…"

children.topic: Knowledge comes down by disciplic succession
children.note: Krishna gave this knowledge to the sun god, and it passed from teacher to disciple; in that chain the knowledge stays guarded and safe. — "the knowledge I'm giving you Arjuna, I had given it to the son god. Son…"
The Sanskrit name for transcendental knowledge: it originates in the spiritual world, not here. — "In Sanskrit it is called dyagyan. Means it is knowledge that is not coming from…"

children.topic: Family recipe passed mother to daughter
children.note: A bunny chow recipe becomes a family recipe by being handed down generation to generation - this is how disciplic succession transmits knowledge. — "Oh, this recipe is a secret recipe of our family and we know how to…"

Everything is learned from someone else; a teacher's authority comes from having received the knowledge from a teacher. — "You cannot have a lecturer teaching at a university and he doesn't have a degree…"

The guru has seen the truth and can explain it, as Prabhupada explains the Gita; otherwise we would rack our brains over it alone. — "just to learn the truth by approaching a special master inquire from and unto him…"
